## v0.4.346 — Direction-independent current-Measure Size control (fully accepted and deployed on main)

**Exact recovery:** Accepted v0.4.345 main `211bd6d95425d778fd4f9dfb67099eaf44e8a1b2`. Work branch `work/v0.4.346-current-measure-size`, candidate `fa26a5461fa093027e61ec1b50b80efa651bd2f4`, one commit ahead with no rollback. The required [ten-job candidate acceptance 39344814204](https://github.com/Diabolicdonut/BECMI-Mystara/actions/runs/39344814204) succeeded in all jobs: two deterministic, four Chromium slices, exact production/native smoke, established Native Acceptance v2, ordered once-only coverage/isolation, and required acceptance gate. Production SHA-256 `b2adcec72a0785c956e56f4f894c6c4aad81560d47ae08ee8cf7ecf5773fa2b8`. The immutable v0.4.333 and candidate Native Acceptance v2 gates remain required; historical 523 evidence remains historical. This candidate is not considered deployed until metadata acceptance CI, reviewed merge, and exact-main/Pages checks pass.

**Rule:** For each actual, eligible opposed melee pair, Far favors the larger Size, Normal favors neither, and Close favors the smaller Size. Size advantage is `min(3, abs(Size difference))` and applies independently of either Press/Hold/Open intention to already existing *unmodified* side-initiative d6 rolls. No reroll or new attack is introduced. Equal die results retain Measure; equal intentions keep their established path. Subsequent changes remain one band per round per pair, with independent six-plus legal opposing contacts. Referee traces may retain numerical control evidence; player narrative remains nonnumeric. The actual source-backed wolf bite is neutral Size 0 when the canonical one-bite 1d6 attack is verified, not generalized to unidentified natural attacks.

**Preserved boundaries:** Surprise and directionally uncovered physically legal first approach can establish Measure without opposed control; physical reach/weapon clearance, casting and disabled status gate eligibility. Unknown initiative dice remain unknown; unusable weapons cannot claim Size advantage. Switching keeps the existing weapon window with no free Measure change. Attack, damage, equipment, encumbrance, withdrawal, saves, and normal modified initiative phase order remain unchanged. Pure Mentzer BECMI RAW bypasses contextual control while retaining inactive facts. All 46 canonical weapon profiles, source natural/special damage, planning-only ship contracts, sparse null/false/zero semantics, older migration and save/reload are preserved.

**Evidence:** Eight added embedded regression definitions, all 36 opposed d6 pairs, all nine intent combinations, three Measure bands, both Size directions and differences 0/1/2/3/5, source-backed spear/swords/dagger/wolf, Open/Hold at Close and sidearm switching, independent six-opponent pairing, surprise, new contact, unknown dice, inaccessible positions, casting/disabled and physically unusable weapon gates, RAW/contextual isolation, migration and repeat save. Dedicated `validation/measure-size-native-v0.4.346.mjs` runs eight embedded definitions plus four actual command/save/reload scenarios. Three historical v0.4.342 native expected values are updated only for superseded intent-dependent restrictions without deleting the twenty case identities or relaxing assertions. Earlier required acceptance gates remain intact. See [current-Measure Size contract](design/context-matrix/CURRENT-MEASURE-SIZE-CONTRACT.md) and [2026-10-19 completion authority](design/context-matrix/CONTEXTUAL-COMBAT-COMPLETION-2026-10-19.md).

Exact staged acceptance metadata `734f443024604144e36021f449633bdb7ca06798` passed ten-job [push 39352549654](https://github.com/Diabolicdonut/BECMI-Mystara/actions/runs/39352549654) and ten-job [PR 39352556014](https://github.com/Diabolicdonut/BECMI-Mystara/actions/runs/39352556014). ## v0.4.345 — Oversized rigid-weapon physical clearance (fully accepted and deployed on main)

**Recovery and exact qualification:** Branched only from fully accepted/deployed v0.4.344 main; its exact promotion evidence is retained in the next audit entry. Final candidate `fab6c24bd6ee1896120d22d91cb9d3ea7bd57174` passed every one of the ten required jobs on [Actions 39311040167](https://github.com/Diabolicdonut/BECMI-Mystara/actions/runs/39311040167). Exact production SHA-256 `c1a1d079bbc1f1fb5d726c83880c06c384ad50f11075b9bcb722fe301b4657fe`. **2340/2340 core, 1256/1256 focused, 585/585 in each of four fresh Chromium processes**, ordered once-only coverage/isolation, exact-production native boot/save-reload and Native Acceptance v2 **33 scenarios / 508/508 on immutable v0.4.333 and candidate**. Historical 523 evidence remains historical and was not rerun.

**Bounded physical policy:** The user-authorized approximately 10-foot rigid-pole dungeon transport benchmark is checked independently from weapon Size, handedness or damage. Compatible supplied RC printed p.65 describes standard pikes as 12-18 feet; that interval proves oversize, and the upper bound is used only to prove a spacious exception when actual length is absent. Explicit actual variant lengths take precedence without silently changing canonical ratings. Explicit long lances and long variants use their actual rigid lengths; no blanket polearm/spear/two-hand ban. Ordinary confined sites require verified route, deployment and attack spans for an oversized weapon. A spacious chamber label or Context Matrix Open space is not sufficient geometric evidence. This is optional contextual feasibility, not a newly asserted printed RAW rule.

**Runtime:** Ordinary keyed entry and movement check actual positive-quantity personal/shared carried items and equipped instances. Refusal spends no travel time/RNG and never silently drops equipment. Transport, deployment and attack permission remain independent. An unusable ordinary manufactured weapon cannot attack, grant a Measure Size advantage or supply weapon approach coverage; refusal precedes its attack/damage dice. Usable damage, attack frequency, normal equipment handling, shields, encumbrance and all 46 profile ratings remain unchanged. Source-specific effects and natural attacks remain separate, with no new damage adjustment. Pure RAW bypasses the new overlay while preserving existing RAW restrictions and inactive contextual facts. Existing fighting withdrawal/retreat has no new compulsory Measure escape contest.

**Persistent facts:** Keyed `weaponClearanceBySite` records and encounter-scoped physical facts keep route/deployment/attack capacities separate from player belief or map presentation. The developer-only explicit recorder validates known keyed sites, nonnegative finite distances or explicit unknown, and a physical source note. Actual item lengths and NPC weapon-ID length maps retain literal unknowns; the optional old-save dictionary defaults only when absent, while supplied null/false/zero originals remain literal. A known equipped single item's length can establish a missing matching inventory length, without assuming the same for an unspecified second item. No source/canonical map geometry is fabricated or mass rewritten.

**Dedicated evidence:** Eight new embedded regressions cover PC/NPC pike attack and Measure/ZOI refusal, standard interval and explicit 12/24-foot spacious exceptions, exact 10-foot benchmark, long lance/poleaxe versus short forms independent of Size, separately scoped transport/deploy/use, no-cost ordinary entry refusal and explicit supported entry, pure RAW versus usable contextual damage/RNG equality, natural exclusion, fighting withdrawal, NPC actual-weapon migration, sparse lengths/facts and repeat migration. The required `rigid-weapon-native-v0.4.345.mjs` gate runs those eight definitions plus native entry refusal, explicit physical-fact command/save/reload and permitted entry, and a refused surprise-period pike attack: **11 scenarios / 26 outer assertions**, plus each embedded assertion, zero page/console/network errors. Actual saved NPC lance identity/length, explicit null PC length, HP, RNG/time, inventory, rule choices and planning-only ship contracts are checked. All 2332 inherited embedded test bodies and the production tail following them are byte-identical to v0.4.344; every prior required combat, coverage, surprise, Context Matrix and native gate remains green.

**Next / promotion:** Exact acceptance-metadata SHA requires full CI before merge, followed by exact merged-main acceptance and Pages verification. This is the third newly accepted game checkpoint of the current continuation once promotion is complete; stop this session after final verification under the repository's three-checkpoint ceiling. Next fresh continuation is **v0.4.346 — current-Measure Size advantage independent of Press/Hold/Open direction**. Far favors longer; Normal neither; Close shorter; min(3, absolute Size difference) plus the existing unmodified initiative d6, no new die. Separate source-reviewed Ferocity +1 and the separate physical natural proximity -1/0/+1 policy follow. Natural attacks never enter the weapon calculator; pure RAW retains printed damage. Do not introduce Docile. Persistent authoritative scene coordinates follow combat dependencies, with no premature graphical map. The full 2026-10-19 user completion contract remains binding. Tests are mechanical/persistence evidence, not a claim of proven gameplay balance.

**Final v0.4.345 promotion:** Acceptance metadata `220e0e33c9675582ff364c7360a284f44053913e` passed all ten required jobs on [push 39312324215](https://github.com/Diabolicdonut/BECMI-Mystara/actions/runs/39312324215) and [PR 39312343409](https://github.com/Diabolicdonut/BECMI-Mystara/actions/runs/39312343409) before [PR #10](https://github.com/Diabolicdonut/BECMI-Mystara/pull/10) merged to `2b0729fed75a0b33a2c747a6fe33dfc58876c191`. Breath, gaze, spells, projectile, Special and unknown-delivery attacks are excluded. Where active threat, legal pursuit or multi-actor attribution cannot be verified—including conflicting intentions or ambiguous connected formations—fail closed to existing unmodified side-initiative Measure resolution, never a fabricated group Size.

## v0.4.231 — Buccaneer/Pirate additional-NPC crossbow ammunition/loading contract

This accepted checkpoint implements the v0.4.230 audit's prescribed additional-NPC counterpart to ordinary crossbow loading. Each supplied loading row identifies an existing additional NPC, an exact carried crossbow item and an instance within that inventory quantity. Remaining allocations are bounded by that NPC's explicit quarrel inventory; heavy cadence reads the NPC's existing explicit Strength. The contract remains planning-only. Development continues automatically after acceptance.

### Baseline, authority and bounded source use

The accepted v0.4.230 implementation is the baseline, with **1280/1280** core tests passing. The current production HTML, newest audit and supplied continuous controller govern chronology. Phase 1 source completion remains active; Mentzer BECM remains primary and compatible Rules Cyclopedia material secondary.

This checkpoint reuses the previously visually reviewed **Rules Cyclopedia printed pp.63–64 / PDF pp.65–66** ammunition/loading facts and the unchanged existing item/class permissions. Quarrels use the existing `quarrels30` inventory identity, with 30 quarrels per recorded pack. Heavy crossbows ordinarily fire every two rounds, with the explicit Strength-18 exception permitting every round. Loading requires two hands. The existing PC firing/reload procedure is unchanged. No source supplies NPC starting stock or individual abilities automatically.

The source Ocean 02–03 / Buccaneer-Pirate / Special route, RC printed p.193 organization and earlier source profiles remain unchanged. Runtime composition is **628 = 600 canonical + 21 supplemental + 7 module profiles**; nonnumeric routes remain **4 live + 1 planning-only ship route**. This is a bounded loading/inventory contract, not a new complete primary-source audit or declaration of BECM closure.

### Explicit instance schema and ammunition conservation

Optional top-level `npcCrossbows` is an array. Rows contain only:

| Field | Explicit contract |
| --- | --- |
| `npcId` | Existing additional leader, captain, commander or present specialist ID; normalized for matching |
| `crossbow` | Exact carried `crossbow_light` or `crossbow_heavy`, permitted by that NPC's existing class rules |
| `instance` | Positive safe integer from 1 through the explicit carried quantity of this item |
| `quarrels` | Nonnegative safe integer remaining allocation, including a loaded quarrel |
| `loaded` | Boolean |
| `reloadPending` | Boolean ordinary heavy-crossbow alternate-round lock |

For example, after those weapons and ammunition have been explicitly recorded in `leader_1`'s inventory:

```json
{"npcCrossbows":[{"npcId":"leader_1","crossbow":"crossbow_light","instance":1,"quarrels":7,"loaded":true,"reloadPending":false},{"npcId":"leader_1","crossbow":"crossbow_light","instance":2,"quarrels":0,"loaded":false,"reloadPending":false}]}
```

Instances distinguish existing carried copies; they do not create objects, default stock or weapon-specific magic effects. Missing instances are reported as counts. Even a large valid inventory quantity produces no enumerated placeholder people/weapons. Duplicate normalized NPC/item/instance references, uncarried items, aliases, ordinary crew IDs and out-of-range instances are refused.

Each NPC's crossbow allocations share a single ceiling: its explicit `quarrels30` inventory quantity multiplied by 30. Loaded shots are already included and never added again. Other NPCs, ordinary crew and party stock cannot satisfy this ceiling. Omitted ammunition inventory establishes zero capacity only when that NPC's inventory is explicitly supplied. Explicit zero allocation is valid with an unloaded weapon. Unallocated capacity is an upper bound; it is **not** declared remaining reserve, refilled stock or a free ammunition grant. Remaining allocations may be lower than original pack capacity.

Exact pack-capacity comparisons use private integer arithmetic. Persisted metadata uses safe numbers where possible and exact decimal strings beyond safe-number bounds; no BigInt reaches JSON/save state. Aggregate supplied remaining stock must remain a safe integer. Earlier valid large inventory quantities are preserved without automatic allocations.

Heavy Strength comes exclusively from the NPC's validated `combat.abilities.str`. The loading row cannot override it. Missing Strength reports `combat.abilities.str`, leaves cadence unresolved and creates no score. Partial stock/flags remain unresolved. The shared loading validator refuses loaded-with-zero-stock, loaded-and-pending, a light heavy-reload lock and a Strength-18 alternate-round lock. Strict booleans/counts, supported source bounds and exact item references remain enforced.

Carrying a weapon does not grant permission to use it. A Magic-User or Cleric may preserve a carried crossbow under the existing possession contract, but it is listed as ineligible for this loading layer and cannot receive a supported loading declaration. Equipped-item permissions and shield/two-handed restrictions remain with the earlier NPC equipment validator. Loading completeness never selects a readied weapon/instance or declares firing readiness.

### Independent readiness, commands and persistence

The plan advances to `contractVersion:7`. Earlier crew, NPC combat, ship allocation, shared weapon, ordinary identity/HP and ordinary loading readiness meanings remain unchanged. New `npcCrossbowLoading` reports known/expected/supplied/configured instances, original recipient/item groups, partial fields, missing inventory/roster decisions, per-NPC capacity/allocation metadata and ineligible carried crossbows. `npcCrossbowsSpecified` and `npcCrossbowContractReady` describe only this bounded independent layer.

Original row order, ordinary HP/IDs/weapons/stock, NPC equipment/enhancements, spellbooks and READY/SPENT entries remain intact.

`liveConstructible:false`, Number Appearing **Special**, `numberTotal:null` and `representedRosterCount:null` are retained even with every current layer configured. ### Explicit schema and source checks

Optional top-level `ordinaryCrossbows` is an array of individual loading records. Its recipients are existing crossbow-bearing `ordinaryTroops` IDs, excluding sword-only people and every additional NPC. IDs are normalized for matching and must be unique. No missing recipient is generated.

| Field | Required explicit value |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Existing crossbow-bearing ordinary troop ID |
| `crossbow` | Exact `crossbow_light` or `crossbow_heavy` already chosen for that person's assigned group |
| `quarrels` | Nonnegative safe integer remaining count, including any loaded quarrel |
| `loaded` | Boolean |
| `reloadPending` | Boolean representing the ordinary heavy-crossbow alternate-round reload lock |
| `strength` | Unmodified integer 3–18, required for heavy crossbows; valid explicit light-crossbow Strength may also be retained |

Example for an already identified crew member in a group whose chosen crossbow is heavy:

```json
{"ordinaryCrossbows":[{"id":"crew_ref_01","crossbow":"crossbow_heavy","quarrels":7,"loaded":false,"reloadPending":true,"strength":17}]}
```

Counts are individual quarrels, not packs. The existing `AMMO_RULES` identity `quarrels30` is retained as catalogue metadata; it grants neither a pack nor 30 shots. A loaded quarrel is part of the supplied count and is not added again. Explicit zero stock is valid with `loaded:false`. Aggregate supplied stock must also remain a safe integer.

Omitted arrays, `[]` and valid partial rows leave missing fields unresolved. Missing heavy Strength produces no default score or firing cadence. A supplied exact item requires an existing matching group choice; aliases, unknown items and silent rebinding are refused. Partial rows may report an unresolved shared crossbow choice without selecting one.

Invalid states are refused: loaded with zero stock; loaded and reload-pending simultaneously; a light crossbow with the heavy reload lock; Strength 18 with that weaker-character lock; coerced booleans/numbers; exceptional Strength; and unsupported pack, action, magical/silver/poison, inventory or recipient overrides. Strength 3–17 gives ordinary cadence 2 rounds; explicit 18 gives 1. This is source cadence metadata, not a promise that a live actor can fire in the current situation. Loading hands remain ordinary source metadata, with no initiative or firing action resolved.

## v0.4.229 — Buccaneer/Pirate explicit ordinary troop identities and HP

### Baseline and bounded source review

The delivered v0.4.228 HTML and its topmost audit govern this checkpoint. Its complete production baseline passed **1250/1250** before editing, with isolation preserved and zero page exceptions or console errors. The preceding audit history is retained verbatim below this entry.

The route remains **DMR2 Creature Catalog, printed p. 120 / PDF p. 121: Ocean 02–03 → Buccaneer/Pirate / Special**, using **Rules Cyclopedia, printed p. 193 / PDF p. 195**. The supplied Rules Cyclopedia's printed **pp. 152 and 193 / PDF pp. 154 and 195** were rendered and visually inspected for the ordinary Hit Dice basis. The troop entry gives **1 HD (M)**; the monster-stat explanation uses d8 for Hit Dice. The unmodified ordinary HP range is therefore **1–8**.

The retained canonical profiles `man_buccaneer` (**EXP-0058**) and `man_pirate` (**EXP-0059**) retain their primary **Mentzer Expert, printed p. 53** identity, HD 1 and existing `hpKind:'1d8'` conversion. The new validator reads these canonical profiles and checks the audited HD/HP basis. It never calls the HP roller or the ordinary encounter loadout generator. The catalogue's older secondary page locator of 194 is left intact; this review uses the inspected Rules Cyclopedia troop table on printed p. 193. Source-data locator normalization is separate from this roster checkpoint.

The retained Mentzer BECM primary authority and compatible Rules Cyclopedia secondary authority remain in force. This is a bounded review of supplied ordinary troop HP material and existing source records, not a new review of the entire primary corpus. Saving as F1 or being described as mostly fighters does not assign a class, Constitution score or exceptional HP bonus to each ordinary planning record.

### Explicit individual roster and conservation

The optional top-level `ordinaryTroops` array supplies individual records:

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Required stable ID, normalized to lowercase for identity; 1–80 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens |
| `shipIndex` | Required explicit integer identifying an already allocated ship |
| `groupKey` | Required exact faction equipment-group key with a positive assigned count on that ship |
| `hp` | Explicit current living HP, integer 1–8; omitted values stay unresolved |
| `maxHp` | Explicit maximum HP, integer 1–8; omitted values stay unresolved |
| `name` | Optional referee-supplied nonempty text, at most 120 characters; never generated or required for completeness |

For example, this supplies one individual in an already assigned pirate sword group; the other assigned people remain missing:

```json
{
  "ordinaryTroops": [
    {
      "id": "crew_ref_01",
      "name": "Rowan",
      "shipIndex": 1,
      "groupKey": "leatherSword",
      "hp": 3,
      "maxHp": 7
    }
  ]
}
```

IDs must be unique within the contract, including every ordinary troop, additional leader, captain, commander and present specialist. Case variants cannot bypass uniqueness. Names are optional labels rather than identity; distinct IDs may have the same name. Normalized derived IDs/names do not alter the original explicit configuration.

Every supplied individual consumes one existing slot in their exact ship/group. A group cannot exceed its assigned count even when other groups still have unidentified people. A complete roster must fill every assigned group exactly and cover the entire ordinary crew; additional NPCs do not consume ordinary slots. Unknown/unallocated ships, zero-count groups, foreign faction keys and malformed targets are refused. Missing people are reported as counts, not invented IDs or placeholder records. Unallocated ships remain unresolved and cannot receive individuals until their groups are explicitly supplied.

An omitted array or explicit `[]` leaves all individual records unresolved. A row with a valid ID/target and partial HP is accepted as an identified person with missing HP fields. Current HP must not exceed the supplied maximum. Each supplied HP field is bounded independently, so omitting `maxHp` cannot admit current HP outside the source range. Strings, booleans, fractions, non-finite values, zero/dead HP and exceptional values above 8 are refused rather than coerced or repaired.

The **positive living HP restriction is this bounded schema's scope**, not a new death or casualty rule. Dead troops, resurrection, extraordinary HP effects and class/Constitution overrides need separately represented state. Unknown per-person fields such as class, level, abilities, alignment, inventory, equipment, magic items, actor flags or profile overrides are refused rather than ignored.

Each derived record points to its existing ship/group through `sharedWeaponChoiceRef`. The group remains the authority for the existing shared sword/crossbow/readied/grip choice. No individual inventory is copied or granted, and no individual loadout variation is silently inferred. Group equipment may still be unresolved while individual identity/HP is complete.

### Independent readiness and atomic updates

The plan advances to `contractVersion:5`. Earlier crew, NPC-detail, ship-allocation and weapon readiness retain their meanings. The new independent fields are:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |

Complete identities/HP do not require or create missing NPC combat details or group weapon choices. Conversely, complete weapons/NPC details do not imply individual roster completeness. Complete records on the supplied ships cannot complete a fleet whose other ship allocations remain unresolved. The existing source ranges still cap these bounded fleets at 240 ordinary crew.

```text
dev dmr2 ship roster crew <contract-id> | <json>
dev dmr2 ship roster crew status <contract-id>
```

The update payload contains only `ordinaryTroops` and replaces that entire array in the existing contract. The original full validator checks the replacement before committing it. Unknown contracts, malformed JSON, invalid fields, duplicate IDs and inconsistent counts/HP leave the prior record intact. Stable contract ID and creation time are preserved.

General roster status reports concise source/group/completeness counts. Dedicated crew status also lists supplied individual IDs, optional names, ship/group references and current/maximum HP, including explicit unresolved fields. Both are read-only and generate no missing records. Literal names/JSON remain protected from natural-language party/group and time interpretation.

NPC, weapon and allocation updates retain the current individual array and revalidate it. Recipient edits that orphan or overfill saved people are refused atomically rather than deleting or moving records. A later additional-NPC ID cannot collide with saved crew IDs. The referee can explicitly clear/reconfigure the array or submit a consistent full contract replacement before changing recipients.

The existing save migration revalidates original configuration and recomputes all derived status/HP/reference data; forged saved plan values are ignored. Original array order, supplied names/HP, NPC item bonuses, spellbooks and READY/SPENT preparations are preserved. Legacy contracts keep identities/HP unresolved. Invalid explicit saved configuration follows the existing contract-refusal policy, without silently repairing individual records. No new migration collection or live actor subsystem is introduced.

### Explicit choices for nonempty assigned groups

The optional top-level `troopWeapons` array contains choices keyed by the existing integer `shipIndex` and exact faction `groupKey`. A target must be a nonempty group in an explicitly supplied ship allocation. Duplicate choices, unallocated/unknown ships, foreign faction groups and zero-count targets are refused. Weapon choices cannot infer ship allocations or add recipients.

Each target represents **one shared weapon choice for all ordinary troops in that assigned ship/group**. This bounded schema does not claim support for individual weapon variation within that count. Such variation needs a separately represented roster/override rather than repeated ambiguous entries or silently split groups.

Required fields are:

| Field | Explicit choice |
| --- | --- |
| `sword` | One of the four exact existing sword IDs |
| `crossbow` | One of the two exact crossbow IDs for a source crossbow group; explicit `null` for a group without one |
| `readied` | `sword`, `crossbow`, or explicit `null` for no readied weapon |
| `swordGrip` | `one` or `two` when a bastard sword is readied; an explicitly chosen carried bastard-sword grip may also be retained |

An omitted field remains unresolved. An empty array records no choices and leaves assigned groups unresolved. Partial rows are accepted when every supplied value is valid. Missing crossbows, normal swords, readied selections and bastard grips are not filled from defaults.

The source categories remain authoritative: a leather/chain sword-only group cannot carry or ready a crossbow through this contract. A crossbow group must explicitly choose its crossbow; `null` cannot remove it. Names/aliases such as `sword`, case variants, other weapons, ammunition IDs, shield weapons and arbitrary item descriptions are refused as exact identities. Foreign fields such as magic bonuses/powers, charges, class overrides, extra shields or offhand weapons are also refused rather than ignored.

For example, a choice for an already assigned nonempty buccaneer crossbow group can be supplied as:

```json
{
  "troopWeapons": [
    {
      "shipIndex": 2,
      "groupKey": "leatherSwordCrossbow",
      "sword": "sword_bastard",
      "swordGrip": "two",
      "crossbow": "crossbow_light",
      "readied": "sword"
    }
  ]
}
```

Carrying both source weapons does not imply using them simultaneously. A single readied selection represents ordinary use; an explicit `null` retains carried weapons without readying one. A carried bastard sword does not require an active grip when another weapon or no weapon is readied. A normal/short/two-handed sword cannot acquire an optional grip override through this schema.

### Reuse of existing equipment rules

Validation uses existing `SHOP_ITEMS`, `classAllowsItem`, `memberItemRecord`, `masteryWeaponKey` and the pure `validateDmr2ShipNpcCombat` equipment path on scratch data. The ordinary source-human equipment template uses existing Fighter equipment permissions for validation; it does not create or assign a class/level to an individual actor.

The source group's leather/chain armor maps to the existing catalogue item ID. Complete explicit choices are checked as one person's carried/readied equipment with that source armor and no added shield. Those scratch records are validation inputs, not granted inventory or a live crew roster. No HP, ability scores, alignment, starting wealth, teacher spells or mastery ranks are generated.

Derived metadata preserves chosen carried weapon IDs, the existing readied item/matrix identity, bastard grip/mastery key, source armor identity, and ordinary readied hand classification. Two-handed swords, crossbows and a two-handed bastard grip use the existing ordinary two-handed metadata. The hand classification is not a claim about every firing step, ammunition, loading, exceptional single-handed use or rate of fire. Those remain governed by the existing procedures when represented live state becomes available. Weapon damage, range and initiative are not newly calculated or replaced here.

### Independent readiness, updates and persistence

The plan advances to `contractVersion:4`. Earlier `contractReady`, `npcCombatContractReady` and `shipTroopAllocationContractReady` meanings remain unchanged. New fields are:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |

| `troopWeaponContractReady` | The existing crew contract and this bounded weapon-choice contract are complete |

Complete weapon rows on a partial ship allocation cannot acquire fleet-wide weapon completeness. An empty set of known recipients never becomes complete. Derived choices follow normalized ship order and the faction's existing group order; original `config.troopWeapons` keeps exact referee row order and decisions.

One command was added to the searchable developer reference:

```text
dev dmr2 ship roster weapons <contract-id> | <json>
```

The payload contains only `troopWeapons` and replaces that entire array in one existing saved contract. The existing full recording validator checks it atomically. Unknown contracts, malformed JSON or invalid choices preserve the old record. General roster status now shows weapon identities, grip, carried/readied distinction, ordinary hands, configured group counts and missing fields without changing state.

Stable contract ID/creation time, fleet/per-ship counts, NPC item bonuses, spellbooks and READY/SPENT preparations remain intact. NPC and allocation update paths retain weapon choices by cloning the latest explicit configuration and using the same validator.

An allocation edit that removes a group with saved weapon choices is refused atomically. It cannot silently discard those choices or move them elsewhere. The referee can explicitly clear/reconfigure the weapon array or submit a consistent full contract replacement before changing recipients.

Save migration revalidates the original configuration, recomputes all derived flags and item identities, and ignores stale/forged plan values. Legacy contracts remain valid with weapon choices unresolved. No additional migration, fleet, inventory or combat subsystem was added. Literal ship-roster JSON continues to bypass natural-language party/group interpretation.

### Baseline and governing source

The delivered v0.4.226 HTML and topmost audit are the baseline. Its complete production suite passed **1220/1220** before editing, with isolation preserved and zero page exceptions or console errors. The direction file's audit chronology and small-checkpoint rules remain in force; older next-step statements are historical.

| Equipment group | Buccaneers | Pirates |
| --- | ---: | ---: |

The source gives troop percentages and men per ship without selecting individual equipment-group placements among ships. This contract preserves v0.4.225's explicitly validated **fleet-wide** counts and rounding provenance. It does not introduce a claim that each individual ship must reproduce the printed percentages. ### Explicit allocation schema and conservation

The optional top-level `troopsByShip` field is an array. Each supplied entry contains only an integer `shipIndex` and a `troops` object with all three faction-specific equipment-group keys. Counts must be nonnegative safe integers, including explicit zeros. Indices are one-based positions in the existing crew list and must identify distinct represented ships.

Each supplied ship's group counts must total **exactly its chosen ordinary crew**. Additional leaders, captains, commanders and present specialists are excluded. A ship allocation cannot alter a crew count, move an NPC, add equipment groups, change source percentages or expand an encounter range.

The sum allocated to any group cannot exceed its existing fleet-wide count, even in a partial allocation. A complete allocation must preserve every fleet group exactly. Fleet counts must already be explicitly supplied and validated; the planner cannot infer them by summing ship rows. The existing fractional-percentage note and adjacent-integer quota rules continue to apply to the fleet contract.

Omitted allocations leave every ship unresolved. An explicit empty array also leaves every ship unresolved while recording that an empty allocation was supplied. A partial array is a valid planning choice when all supplied rows are valid. Its remaining fleet counts are diagnostics; the validator does not choose a missing ship, rounding method or equipment recipient.

For the existing 60-buccaneer example, a deliberately uneven allocation is valid:

```json
{
  "troopsByShip": [
    {"shipIndex": 1, "troops": {"leatherSword": 20, "leatherSwordCrossbow": 0, "chainSwordCrossbow": 0}},
    {"shipIndex": 2, "troops": {"leatherSword": 16, "leatherSwordCrossbow": 18, "chainSwordCrossbow": 6}}
  ]
}
```

Ship 1 has 20 ordinary crew, ship 2 has 40, and the totals remain 36/18/6. Supplying only ship 2 reports ship 1 as missing and 20/0/0 as unallocated; it does not create the omitted row automatically.

Malformed containers or rows, unknown fields, duplicate/out-of-range indices, omitted faction keys, foreign equipment groups, booleans/string/fractional counts, incorrect ship totals and oversubscribed fleet groups refuse the entire operation rather than discarding or coercing entries.

| `contractReady` | Existing ordinary crew, fleet equipment, leadership and specialist choices are complete |
| `npcCombatContractReady` | Existing crew contract and every supported individual NPC detail contract are complete |
| `shipTroopAllocations` | Supplied ship rows, configured/total ship counts, missing indices, allocated and remaining fleet group counts, and allocation basis |
| `shipTroopAllocationsSpecified` | Every ship allocation is complete and conserves validated fleet counts |
| `shipTroopAllocationContractReady` | Existing crew contract and the per-ship allocation contract are both complete |
| `liveConstructible` | Always `false` for this ship route |

The derived `troopsByShip` rows are sorted by ship index for inspection and include each ship's ordinary crew count. The original `config.troopsByShip` retains the referee's exact row order and choices. No physical vessel identity or actor state is invented from these indices.

One command was added to the searchable developer reference:

```text
dev dmr2 ship roster troops <contract-id> | <json>
```

Its payload contains only `troopsByShip`. It replaces the entire allocation array in one existing saved contract, then revalidates that contract through the existing recording path. A partial replacement deliberately reopens allocation readiness; it does not merge omitted rows from an earlier allocation. An unknown contract, malformed JSON or invalid allocation preserves the old record atomically.

The existing `dev dmr2 ship roster status <contract-id>` now displays per-ship counts, configured/total ships, missing indices and unallocated fleet counts alongside fleet and NPC details. Inspection remains read-only. Ship-roster JSON continues to bypass natural-language party interpretation, so literal strings cannot execute group or time instructions.

Stable contract ID and creation time are preserved on replacement. Allocation updates retain all NPC combat details, item bonuses, spellbooks and READY/SPENT preparations. Existing NPC-detail updates retain allocations because both paths clone the latest explicit configuration and use the same full validator.

Save migration revalidates original configurations and recomputes all derived allocation flags/counts without dice. Stale or forged saved plan rows cannot supply missing configuration. Legacy v0.4.225/v0.4.226 contracts remain valid with unresolved ship allocations; no new migration subsystem or default distribution was added.

### Live and architectural boundaries

Even with all NPC details and ship allocations configured, the route remains planning-only. Number Appearing is still `Special`, with `numberTotal:null` and `representedRosterCount:null`. Generic DMR2 construction cannot bypass this boundary using a fully configured contract. The five nonnumeric routes remain **4 live source-specific routes + 1 planning-only ship route**.

Equipment-group labels are counts of the source categories, not complete individual inventory/weapon state. Exact sword/crossbow identities and grip/hand choices, individual ordinary-troop HP and other combat details, unsupported magic-item state, hull/vessel configuration, prisoners, treasure, surprise, distance and naval procedures remain separate work. The contract creates no party members, combatants, ships, inventory items, RNG draws, time advances or wandering checks. Kai Besil's fixed Pirate Camp/Sorrowful Gull behavior is unchanged.

This extends the existing saved planning collection and source validator. It adds no parallel fleet, inventory, combat or persistence engine. A later live adapter should consume validated choices through existing actor/equipment/combat procedures after the remaining source requirements are represented.

Passing this checkpoint does not declare the full BECM project complete.

### Baseline and source review

The delivered v0.4.225 HTML and topmost audit are the baseline. Before editing, its complete production suite passed **1205/1205**, with isolation preserved and zero page exceptions or console errors. The older next-step statements remain historical under the direction file's chronology rule.

Existing four ship-type ranges and the 240-ordinary-man maximum are preserved. Pirate Lord/Magic-User conditions for 300+ remain visible but cannot enlarge those ranges.

The supplied Rules Cyclopedia class tables were also rendered and inspected for this detail pass:

| Fighter | 16 / 18 | d8 through level 9; +2 HP per later level without Constitution adjustment; class equipment permissions |
| Magic-User | 19 / 21 | d4 through level 9; +1 HP per later level without Constitution adjustment; class equipment restrictions; level-10 slots 3/3/3/3/2 and level-11 slots 4/3/3/3/2/1 |

The retained Mentzer BECM primary authority and compatible Rules Cyclopedia secondary authority remain unchanged. This pass checks the supplied route/class material and reuses the engine's existing core validators; it does not claim a fresh review of the entire primary corpus. Equipment identities, encumbrance, class restrictions, spell catalogues/exclusions, saving-throw bands, and slot tables remain the existing engine rule data.

### Separate readiness and explicit details

Each existing leadership or present-specialist record may contain a nested `combat` object. The saved contract's original `config` retains the referee's exact payload, while its `plan` carries the validated/normalized detail data and derived values. Source class and level still come from the existing leadership/specialist contract and cannot be replaced through `combat`.

Legacy v0.4.225 crew contracts remain valid without combat objects. Partial combat objects are also valid planning choices when every supplied value is valid. Missing choices are listed rather than generated. Invalid supplied values refuse the entire preview or replacement, preserving an existing saved record atomically.

The plan now has `contractVersion:2` and the following distinct flags:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `contractReady` | The existing ordinary crew, leadership and specialist decision contract is complete; its earlier meaning is preserved |
| `npcCombatDetails` | Total/configured individual NPC counts and missing fields by stable NPC ID |
| `npcCombatDetailsSpecified` | Every supplied individual NPC has complete validated combat choices |
| `npcCombatContractReady` | Both the crew contract and all individual NPC detail contracts are complete |
| `liveConstructible` | Always `false` for this route |

Completeness requires explicit `hp`, `maxHp`, all six `abilities`, `alignment`, `inventory`, `equipment`, `magicItems`, and `spells`. An empty array or explicit `null` is meaningful where allowed; an omitted field remains unresolved. An empty NPC set never acquires NPC-detail completeness.

### HP, abilities and ordinary equipment

HP values must be positive safe integers for a living NPC, with current HP no greater than maximum HP. All six ability scores must be integers from 3 through 18. Maximum HP must fit the existing class Hit Dice/Constitution range at the source level: the first nine levels use class dice and Constitution adjustment with the existing one-HP minimum per die; later fixed gains receive no Constitution adjustment. These are validation bounds, not HP rolls or inferred averages. Exceptional abilities, extra HP effects, and dead/unconscious NPC representation need their own represented state.

Alignment is explicitly Lawful, Neutral or Chaotic. The source's faction tendencies do not choose an individual's alignment or optional high-level Fighter features.

Inventory entries use exact existing `SHOP_ITEMS` IDs, unique entries, and explicit positive quantities. Canonical encumbrance cannot be overridden. A catalogue item with source-silent encumbrance, such as Giant Snail Shell Shield, requires an explicit nonnegative encumbrance choice. Quantity/encumbrance totals must remain safe integers. No item is purchased, granted, or randomly generated.

Readied weapon, armor and shield selections are explicit IDs or `null`. A selected item must be carried and permitted by the existing class rules. Class-restricted spare loot may be carried; it cannot be readied. A bastard sword requires an explicit one- or two-handed grip. An ordinary readied shield cannot coexist with a two-handed weapon. Mastery shield weapons require a separate hand-state contract and are refused in this ordinary-equipment schema.

The validator reuses `memberItemRecord`, `classAllowsItem`, `recalcMemberAc` and `classSaveValues` on scratch records. Complete explicit Dexterity/armor/shield choices yield static ordinary AC. Base class saves are labelled as such; no active-effect, magic-save, or situational modifier is asserted.

### Bounded magic equipment and explicit caster choices

`magicItems:[]` explicitly declares no supported magic equipment. This checkpoint accepts only a declared **+1 through +5 weapon, armor or ordinary shield enhancement** identified by an existing carried item ID. An enhanced item must be one distinct inventory item, not an ambiguous stack. Repeated declarations are refused. The existing magic-item classifier validates the enhancement record; armor/shield bonuses adjust derived AC, while weapon bonuses remain recorded for a later live adapter.

This is **not a full magic-item state contract**. Named powers, curses, potions/consumables, charged devices and other item effects are refused rather than silently accepted as combat-ready. Their ownership, charges, effect state and other source-specific choices require a separate validated extension. The bounded completeness flag therefore means complete for this declared supported schema, not that arbitrary magical NPC loadouts can already be instantiated.

Fighters must explicitly declare `spells:null`; alignment or source level does not grant a divine spell loadout. Magic-Users explicitly supply both `spellbook` and `prepared` arrays. Clerics explicitly supply `prepared`; their class catalogue supplies eligibility, not a chosen preparation list.

Every prepared entry names a spell and explicitly supplies `ready:true` or `false`. The existing source spell level is derived; user-supplied levels and other foreign fields are refused. Ready and spent entries both count against the existing level-specific capacity. Unknown, wrong-class, source-excluded, unavailable-level, over-capacity and repeated spellbook choices are refused. A Magic-User preparation must be permitted by the explicitly supplied book. Unfilled slots remain unfilled. An explicit empty book/preparation list remains empty; Read Magic, teacher additions, starting spells and rest recovery are never inferred.

Magic-User reversed names require the corresponding base spell knowledge and retain the explicit prepared choice. Clerics prepare the base spell and select a permitted reversal when casting, following the existing engine model; reversed cleric preparation names are refused. Optional special preparation modes outside the existing core catalogue are not introduced here.

### Commands, save continuity and live boundaries

Two commands were added to the searchable developer reference:

```text
dev dmr2 ship roster npc <contract-id> <npc-id> | <json>
dev dmr2 ship roster npc status <contract-id> <npc-id>
```

The first replaces one existing NPC's detail object in a saved crew contract, then revalidates the entire contract through the existing recording path. Unknown contract/NPC IDs, malformed JSON or invalid choices leave the old record intact. The second is read-only and shows explicit HP/abilities/alignment, carried/readied items, supported enhancements, spellbook and READY/SPENT preparations, ordinary AC, base class saves and unresolved fields. General roster status now also shows NPC detail counts and per-NPC HP/AC when complete.

For example, the following payload supplies an ordinary Fighter's choices after the first command's separator. It does not change that NPC's source class/level:

```json
{
  "hp": 15,
  "maxHp": 16,
  "abilities": {"str": 10, "int": 12, "wis": 12, "dex": 14, "con": 10, "cha": 10},
  "alignment": "Neutral",
  "inventory": [{"itemId": "sword_normal", "qty": 1}, {"itemId": "chain", "qty": 1}, {"itemId": "shield", "qty": 1}],
  "equipment": {"weapon": "sword_normal", "armor": "chain", "shield": "shield"},
  "magicItems": [],
  "spells": null
}
```

All ship-roster JSON continues to bypass natural-language party interpretation. NPC names and other literal strings cannot execute embedded party/group/time instructions. The commands generate no wealth, HP/ability dice, teacher spells, chance rolls, surprise or distance.

Existing save migration revalidates retained contracts from their original explicit configurations. It recomputes completeness/derived values and ignores stale or forged plan flags without altering stable identities, chosen item bonuses, books, or spent preparations. No separate actor/migration subsystem was added.

Even with every individual NPC configured, generic live encounter construction still refuses this ship route. Number Appearing remains `Special`, with no fabricated numeric total or represented roster. The five nonnumeric routes remain **4 live source-specific routes + 1 planning-only ship route**. Recording changes only saved planning metadata: no party members, ships/hulls, combatants, treasure, encounter procedure, time advance, wandering cadence or RNG draw. Kai Besil's existing Pirate Camp/Sorrowful Gull procedure is unchanged.

## v0.4.225 — DMR2 Buccaneer/Pirate explicit referee crew/leadership contract

This checkpoint completes **only the explicit roster-contract pass** named by the v0.4.224 audit. The existing ship/crew planner now accepts and validates exact ordinary-crew equipment counts, individual leader/captain/commander records, explicit pirate leadership counting bases, and eligible specialist decisions. A complete contract can be recorded, inspected, replaced, and saved. It is **planning metadata**, not a live ship, combatant, encounter, or naval procedure.

Runtime creature composition stays **628 = 600 canonical + 21 supplemental source profiles + 7 module extensions**. No canonical creature data, wilderness table row/range, encounter cadence, new-campaign rule default, cartography, or ordinary combat procedure changes. Source-completion work remains separate from the later RAW-default, UI, and architecture checkpoints. This acceptance does not declare the full BECM project complete.

### Baseline and governing sources

The delivered v0.4.224 HTML and topmost audit are the baseline. Its full production suite passed **1190/1190**, with isolation preserved and no page/runtime exceptions or console errors, before this checkpoint was implemented. The direction file's older explicit v0.4.224 instruction is satisfied by that completed checkpoint; the topmost audit supplies the current next step under its chronology rule.

The governing route was checked against **DMR2 Creature Catalog, printed p. 120 / PDF p. 121**, and its creature index reference to the **Rules Cyclopedia, printed p. 193 / PDF p. 195**. Both governing table/procedure pages were rendered and inspected. DMR2 Ocean **02–03 → Buccaneer/Pirate / Special** remains unchanged. The retained Mentzer BECM primary authority and compatible Rules Cyclopedia secondary authority remain unchanged for core rules; this pass checks this source route, not the entire primary corpus again.

Printed encounter limits remain:

| Chosen ship type | Ships | Ordinary men per ship |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| River Boat | 1–8 | 10–20 |
| Small Galley | 1–6 | 20–40 |
| Long Ship | 1–4 | 30–50 |
| Sailed Warship | 1–3 | 40–80 |

The source supplies ranges, not a random distribution for choosing these counts. The referee must choose one appropriate ship type and every represented ship's ordinary crew count.

| Ordinary troop equipment | Buccaneers | Pirates |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Leather armor, sword | 60% | 50% |
| Leather armor, sword, crossbow | 30% | 35% |
| Chain mail, sword | — | 15% |
| Chain mail, sword, crossbow | 10% | — |

Buccaneers have an additional Fighter-4 leader per 30 ordinary men, a Fighter-7 captain per ship, and a Fighter-9 fleet commander. Optional specialists retain the printed **30%** Magic-User-10/11 and **25%** Cleric-8 chances.

Pirates have an additional Fighter-4 leader per 30 ordinary men, a Fighter-5 captain per 50 pirates **or one ship**, and a Fighter-8 commander per 100 pirates **or one fleet**. The source separately specifies a Fighter-11 Pirate Lord commanding fleets of 300+ pirates and a **75%** chance of a Magic-User-9/10 for such fleets. Those conditions remain recorded. Under the four **single chosen ship-type** ranges above, the largest possible ordinary crew is **240**, so this contract cannot reach 300 by silently enlarging a ship's crew or combining the independent range rows. Larger/mixed fleets require a separate source-bounded design decision.

The source also gives possible pirate prisoners, fleet-level treasure, and other context. Those remain annotations/boundaries rather than newly generated prisoners, wealth, hull statistics, or scenarios in this crew/leadership checkpoint.

### Strict configuration and explicit integer troop groups

The existing `dmr2BuccaneerPirateRosterPlan(config)` accepts its prior ship and crew aliases. It now refuses malformed comma-separated entries, empty entries, noninteger/boolean counts, foreign fields, and conflicting aliases. The former parser could discard an invalid token from a crew string; the new parser refuses the entire input instead.

Partial plans remain valid previews with `contractReady:false` and a list of missing configuration. They do not fill in equipment, leaders, specialist absence, or dice results.

The optional `troops` object must use exactly the faction's three equipment-group keys. Counts must be nonnegative integers totaling the **ordinary crew only**, excluding additional NPCs. Integer percentage quotas must match exactly. When the percentages produce fractional people, the referee must supply both the exact counts and a nonempty `troopRoundingNote`.

The validator accepts an adjacent lower/upper integer for each fractional quota, with the exact overall total. That is a **contract validation constraint**, not a newly asserted source rounding rule: the engine chooses no allocation method or leftover recipient. For example, 61 pirates give source quotas 30.5/21.35/9.15. Both 31/21/9 and 30/22/9 can be accepted when explicitly supplied and explained; 61/0/0 cannot replace the printed percentages through a note.

Troop groups are scoped to the **entire ordinary crew**. No distribution of those equipment groups across individual ships is inferred.

### Explicit individual leadership records and counting bases

Each supplied NPC record requires a unique stable `id`, explicit `className`, and explicit source `level`. An optional `name` and `shipIndex` can identify the individual and their ship. IDs are normalized to lowercase and remain unique across all leaders and present specialists. Foreign NPC fields, incorrect class/level, out-of-range ship assignments, or repeated identities are refused.

The leadership object requires explicit `leaders`, `captains`, and `commanders` arrays. The contract checks additional Fighter-4 leaders against complete **fleet-wide groups of 30 ordinary crew**. It does not count added leaders back into the ordinary crew or recursively generate leaders.

Buccaneer counting bases are explicitly `captainBasis:'per_ship'` and `commanderBasis:'per_fleet'`. Pirate contracts must explicitly select the printed alternatives: `per_ship` or `per_50` for captains, and `per_fleet` or `per_100` for commanders. Per-ship captain records must cover every ship exactly once.

Selecting a per-men pirate basis requires a `leadership.rulingNote`. The bounded contract counts complete fleet-wide groups with at least one captain/commander under the source's single-ship/fleet alternative. This interpretation is disclosed and referee-selected; it is not an automatic claim that the printed alternatives universally resolve partial groups or ship placement this way. Supplied record counts must match the selected basis, and class levels remain source-defined.

No NPC HP, ability scores, AC, weapon choice, magic item, spell selection, or XP is generated. Those combat details are explicitly unresolved; a configured leadership contract does not imply a ready NPC combat roster.

### Specialist decisions without automatic chance rolls

Buccaneer configurations explicitly supply `specialists.magicUser` and `specialists.cleric`, each with `present:true` or `false`. Presence requires an explicit NPC record of the printed class and allowed level; absence cannot also contain an NPC. Source chances and `chanceRolled:false` remain in the resulting plan.

For source-bounded pirate crews below 300 ordinary men, an explicit empty `specialists:{}` confirms that the referee reviewed the conditional specialist rules. The resulting decisions report **not applicable**, rather than a failed chance roll or an assumed optional caster. A pirate caster below the printed threshold, or an optional pirate cleric not supplied by this source, is refused. The 300+ condition remains visible in the source-rule metadata even though it cannot be reached by enlarging these encounter ranges.

### Referee commands and saved planning records

Three commands are registered in the live searchable developer reference:

```text
dev dmr2 ship roster plan <json>
dev dmr2 ship roster record <stable-id> | <json>
dev dmr2 ship roster status [stable-id]
```

`plan` is a pure preview. `record` accepts only a complete valid configuration. It records or explicitly replaces one stable entry in `state.dmr2ShipRosterContracts`; an invalid replacement leaves the previous entry intact. `status` lists contracts or shows a named contract's ordinary crew, troop counts, leadership records, source chances, readiness, and outstanding live-construction boundaries.

An incomplete preview example:

```text
dev dmr2 ship roster plan {"faction":"pirate","ship":"small_galley","crew":[20,20]}
```

A complete two-ship, 40-pirate configuration can be supplied as the JSON payload below. In the command form, use this as one JSON object after `record example_fleet |`:

```json
{
  "faction": "pirate",
  "ship": "small_galley",
  "crew": [20, 20],
  "tableRoll": 2,
  "troops": {"leatherSword": 20, "leatherSwordCrossbow": 14, "chainSword": 6},
  "leadership": {
    "captainBasis": "per_ship",
    "commanderBasis": "per_fleet",
    "leaders": [{"id": "leader_1", "className": "Fighter", "level": 4}],
    "captains": [
      {"id": "captain_1", "className": "Fighter", "level": 5, "shipIndex": 1},
      {"id": "captain_2", "className": "Fighter", "level": 5, "shipIndex": 2}
    ],
    "commanders": [{"id": "commander", "className": "Fighter", "level": 8}]
  },
  "specialists": {}
}
```

The optional standalone `tableRoll` is restricted to 2 or 3. When reviewing an actual DMR2 Ocean result, the planner inherits that actual roll and refuses conflicting supplied provenance. A standalone preview with no known roll retains `roll:null`; no roll is fabricated.

The source metadata keeps separate DMR2 table and Rules Cyclopedia creature references. `numberExpression:'Special'`, `numberTotal:null`, and `representedRosterCount:null` remain unchanged. The ordinary-crew configuration and additional NPC count are planning quantities, not a rewritten numeric Number Appearing result or a spawned roster.

Ship-roster JSON is routed directly to the developer registry before natural-language party organization/clarification parsing. NPC names and referee notes remain literal data, even if they contain text such as “form everyone into group raiders and then wait.” Such text cannot form a party group or consume time.

Save migration revalidates each retained contract from its original explicit configuration, recomputes its derived plan without dice, and preserves valid choices and stable identity. Invalid, incomplete, or duplicate saved records cannot acquire readiness by trusting stored flags. Older campaigns get an empty contract collection; their existing rule choices remain intact.

### Live-construction and architecture boundaries

Both partial and complete plans retain `liveConstructible:false` and `npcCombatDetailsSpecified:false`. Generic DMR2 encounter construction refuses the Buccaneer/Pirate route and directs the referee to the contract commands. It cannot bypass unresolved NPC details by selecting the existing `man_pirate` or `man_buccaneer` profile.

Recording changes only the planning collection. It creates no combat state, monsters, ships, hull points, party member, treasure, encounter distance, surprise, time advance, wandering check, or RNG draw. It does not replace Kai Besil's fixed Pirate Camp/Sorrowful Gull scenario or cadence.

The five nonnumeric wilderness routes remain **4 live source-specific routes + 1 planning-only ship route**, with Ghostly Horde's dynamic count describing one of the four live routes. The saved metadata is a configuration record for a later adapter, not a parallel naval/combat engine. Later implementation should consume it through the existing source-profile, equipment, NPC, and combat procedures.

## v0.4.224 — DMR2 Ghostly Horde staged personal fear/illusion adapter

This checkpoint implements **only the Ghostly Horde procedure** named by the v0.4.223 audit and the synchronized long-term direction. It adds no creature profile, changes no DMR2 table range or Number Appearing expression, and leaves runtime composition at **628 = 600 canonical + 21 supplemental source profiles + 7 module extensions**. Buccaneer/Pirate, new-campaign RAW defaults, cartography, UI restructuring, autonomous adventurers, and hosted service work are separate checkpoints.

### Review and baseline

The supplied HTML, topmost audit, and direction file agree at **0.4.223**. The direction's chronology rule governs: older counts, completion statements, and next-checkpoint sections below remain historical. Before editing, the complete production baseline passed **1180/1180** tests in fresh Chromium, with campaign isolation preserved and zero page exceptions or console errors.

The current design correctly keeps deterministic rules/state authority separate from referee interpretation. This pass extends the existing `wildernessHazards` registry and character records rather than creating an unrelated combat, movement, mapping, or agency subsystem. The reference engine remains a single-file implementation; architectural separation and campaign endurance validation remain later gates. Passing this checkpoint does **not** declare the full BECM project complete.

### Source verification

The governing entry was checked against **DMR2 Creature Catalog, printed pp. 48–49 / PDF pp. 49–50**, including rendered-page inspection. AC9's matching Ghostly Horde text was also checked for consistency; DMR2 governs this adapter. Retained Mentzer primary authority and compatible Rules Cyclopedia secondary authority remain unchanged for ordinary core procedures; the entire primary corpus was not re-audited in this checkpoint.

The source gives AC **4**, **3 HD**, movement **120' (40')**, one weapon attack, **Damage: By weapon**, **Number Appearing: Special**, Fighter-3 saves, Morale **12**, no treasure, and no XP. A qualifying location is a deserted battlefield, or a city/town where an army suffered sudden catastrophic defeat. Its apparent soldiers may number hundreds or thousands, but only **one soldier attacks each panicked character**.

Each entering character follows the successive **Saving Throw vs. Magic Wands** procedure:

1. First failure: that character sees the horde appear.
2. Second failure: that character sees it prepare to charge.
3. Third failure: that character succumbs to fear and receives one personal soldier.

A successful first save means the character never sees it; a successful second or third save makes it fade. The sequence closes at that success rather than rolling unnecessary later saves. A struck character makes another Wands save; failure causes apparent death through unconsciousness, followed by revival in **1d4 turns**. A character who defeats their soldier never sees the horde again **on that battlefield**.

### Stable battlefield construction, never a fixed army

The DMR2 Ruins d100 result remains **37 → Ghostly Horde / Special**. An explicit referee construction hook establishes a persistent battlefield effect:

```text
dev dmr2 construct ruins 37 | battlefield=<stable-id>
```

The ID must identify the actual qualifying battlefield, be 1–80 letters/digits/underscores/hyphens, and be reused on later visits. It is normalized to lowercase. No identity is inferred from the current hex or table roll. Constructing the same ID reuses the existing record without resetting its participants or history.

The record resides in `state.wildernessHazards` with `kind:'dmr2_ghostly_horde'`. Construction creates **zero soldiers**, makes no entry saves, moves no character, starts no ordinary combat, advances no time, rolls no distance or surprise, and changes no wandering-check cadence. Source provenance retains `numberExpression:'Special'`, `numberTotal:null`, `representedRosterCount:null`, and `fixedUpfrontRoster:false`, with separate table and creature page references.

### Explicit individual entry and successive saves

```text
dev dmr2 ghostly horde enter <character> [| battlefield=<id>]
dev dmr2 ghostly horde fear <character> [| battlefield=<id>]
```

`enter` records an actual referee-confirmed entry and initializes stage zero. Each `fear` command resolves **one** next save through the existing `pcSave(...,'wands',...)` path, including applicable existing saving modifiers. Stage timing is not invented. Per-character state records `entered`, `appeared`, `charging`, `panicked`, or `dismissed`, visibility, save outcomes, visit number, and personal soldier identity.

Repeated `enter` while the same visit remains recorded does not reset the sequence. Closed sequences do not reroll or generate another soldier. A character with a prior victory on this battlefield is marked immune and sees no horde; no entry save is rolled. Ambiguous battlefield selection is refused when multiple records exist, and a character cannot be recorded as simultaneously entering two battlefields.

Only the third failed save creates the personal soldier. It uses the printed AC/HD/movement/morale, existing BECMI 3-HD attack calculation and **3d8** hit-point procedure, Fighter-3 saves, and zero XP. It remains inside that character's battlefield participant record, outside `state.combat.monsters`; there is no shared hundreds/thousands roster.

### Personal attacks and hit-to-unconscious resolution

```text
dev dmr2 ghostly horde strike <character> [| battlefield=<id>]
dev dmr2 ghostly horde hit <character> [| battlefield=<id>]
dev dmr2 ghostly horde attack <character> [| battlefield=<id>]
dev dmr2 ghostly horde damage <character> <damage> [| battlefield=<id>]
```

`strike` resolves one referee-authorized soldier weapon attack using the ordinary 3-HD attack roll against its own character. A miss rolls no Wands save. `hit` represents an already-adjudicated successful hit and resolves only the source's additional Wands-save procedure. Failure creates `ghostlyHordeUnconscious`, not actual death or an invented physical HP loss. Recovery is rolled once as 1d4 turns; repeated hit calls while the victim is down cannot extend or reroll it.

The stat block's **By weapon** damage label is retained. This adapter does not invent the lost army's weapon loadout or a physical-damage interpretation for a panicked-mind illusion. Its automated hit result is the source's explicit saving throw/unconsciousness procedure; other adjudicated consequences remain referee-owned.

`attack` reuses the existing ordinary melee weapon procedure, including the chosen RAW/Matrix damage mode, or the existing ordinary unarmed calculation. A narrowly scoped `damageMonster` bridge applies that character's damage to their personal illusion and records the source-defined victory. It does not create a second combat state. `damage` records already-adjudicated damage from the named character to their own soldier. Cross-character attacks cannot silently grant another character's personal victory.

Attack opportunities, reach, entry/exit, cavalry depiction, and battlefield geometry remain referee-adjudicated. These developer hooks are not an automatic combat scheduler, missile/spell-targeting layer, or new exploration-positioning system.

### Recovery, save continuity, and battlefield memory

Unconsciousness blocks movement, attacks, and spellcasting through existing action checks and appears as **UNCONSCIOUS** on the party panel and character listing. Successful referee actions now refresh the party panel immediately; the native command-flow check caught and verified the refresh fix. Its timer advances through campaign minutes and combat rounds, with **60 rounds = 1 turn = 10 minutes**. Already-counted round time reduces the remaining clock deadline; subsequent exploration does not charge that interval again. Midnight crossings retain the absolute deadline.

Natural recovery clears only the Ghostly Horde cause. It does not clear independent Agarat/Water Weird/other represented unconsciousness, restore lost real HP, resurrect actual death, or award battlefield immunity. The source does not specify a new attack sequence after revival, so post-recovery re-engagement is explicitly left for referee adjudication rather than automatically respawning or restarting a soldier.

Defeating the soldier stores a persistent `ghostlyHordeVictories` record on **that character** keyed to **that battlefield**. No XP or treasure is awarded. Successful entry saves, natural recovery, and leaving the field do not grant this victory memory.

```text
dev dmr2 ghostly horde leave <character> [| battlefield=<id>]
dev dmr2 ghostly horde status [battlefield-id]
```

`leave` records a referee-adjudicated exit and deactivates the current personal engagement, without shortening unconsciousness or awarding victory. Later entry is a new visit. `status` exposes the referee's participant stages, personal soldier HP, recovery, and immunity. New character effects and victory records survive `normalizeMember()` and ordinary save migration; the battlefield registry retains mid-sequence perception, soldier wounds, visit state, and history.

### Nonnumeric source review and architectural implications

The existing five nonnumeric DMR2 routes remain exactly five. The review now reports **4 source-specific live construction routes**, including the conditional Ghostly Horde battlefield path, **1 plan-only Buccaneer/Pirate route**, and **1 dynamic illusion route**. The dynamic count describes the Ghostly Horde subset of the four live routes; it is not an additional sixth source row. No `Special` or `n/a` value becomes a fabricated Number Appearing total.

Future local scenes can consume these existing battlefield effects, per-character perceptions, and victory IDs. They should not replace them with an independently generated army or parallel combat coordinates. Current party-global visibility remains a separate architectural migration; the new personal records do not claim to implement that full renderer/knowledge system.

### Regression and browser acceptance

Ten deterministic v0.4.224 regressions cover explicit battlefield construction/provenance, staged failed and successful Wands saves, one soldier per panicked character, personal perception and ambiguous-field refusal, hit/miss saves and recovery, action locks, midnight and mixed clock/round recovery, independent unconsciousness/actual death, individual battlefield victory and zero XP/loot, ordinary RAW/Matrix/unarmed attacks, save migration, and command routing/malformed-option refusal.

Final production acceptance:

- **1190/1190** complete core tests pass; `isolationPreserved:true`.
- Four independent fresh-Chromium slices pass **298/298**, **298/298**, **298/298**, and **296/296**, covering all 1190 tests again; every slice preserves isolation.
- The related DMR2 focused suite passes **27/27**.
- The uninstrumented production JavaScript boots successfully.
- All accepted runs report **0** page/runtime exceptions and **0** console errors.
- A separate native command-form flow on the uninstrumented production HTML verifies immediate unconsciousness display, actual LocalStorage save/reload with the timer unchanged, recovery through `wait`, and saved battlefield victory immunity on revisiting. It reports zero page exceptions and console errors.
- Extracted production JavaScript passes `node --check`.
- Delivered HTML contains no temporary `__kwValidation`, `__kwHarness`, `__KW_TEST__`, or `__KW_SLICE__` instrumentation.

Regression runs load the exact production HTML shell and inline JavaScript into Chromium. Only independent slice/focused runners expose extra test helpers in temporary copies; the full suite uses the existing production `KnownWorldTestHarness` interface.

Preserve printed ship/crew ranges, troop percentages, and leadership rules. ## v0.4.223 — DMR2 Grab Grass area-contact hazard adapter

This bounded checkpoint implements **only the Grab Grass area/contact procedure** identified but deliberately left non-live in v0.4.222. It adds no creature profile, changes no DMR2 d100 range, does not turn `No. Appearing: Not Applicable` into a monster count, and does not alter wilderness encounter-check cadence. Runtime creature composition therefore remains **628 = 600 canonical + 21 supplemental source profiles + 7 module extensions**.

### Source procedure preserved as an area hazard, not an ordinary creature roster

The Rules Cyclopedia gives Grab Grass **AC 9**, **1 Hit Die per 5-foot square**, Move 0, Damage Special, **No. Appearing: Not Applicable**, Normal Man saves, Morale 12, Intelligence 0, Neutral alignment, and 10 XP. It attempts to hold any individual who moves into or through it. A held individual with Strength 12 or less has a **5% chance per round** to break free; each point of Strength above 12 adds another 5 percentage points. The patch has 1 HD for every 5-foot square, and **8 points of damage destroy one 5-foot square**. Rules Cyclopedia terrain is Hill, Jungle, and Open (printed p. 181 / PDF p. 183).

The DMR2 Jungle wilderness table still contributes only the source result **Grab Grass / `n/a`**. Because neither source supplies a total wilderness patch extent, construction now requires an explicit referee value:

```text
dev dmr2 construct jungle <Grab-Grass d100 result> | squares=<positive integer>
```

The exact d100 result remains whatever was already rolled or explicitly selected. `squares=` defines the represented number of 5-foot squares; it is **not** rewritten as Number Appearing. The resulting source metadata therefore retains `numberExpression:'n/a'`, `numberTotal:null`, and `representedRosterCount:null`.

### Separate persistent wilderness-hazard state

A constructed patch is stored in `state.wildernessHazards` as a `dmr2_grab_grass` area hazard rather than being inserted into `state.combat.monsters`. Each represented 5-foot square carries its own 8 hp and destroyed/not-destroyed state. The patch records its total 5-foot-square extent, total represented area, corresponding Hit Dice, AC 9, DMR2 source route, and damage/contact history.

This keeps the source model intact: the grass is a spatial obstacle with per-square durability, not a bag of identical monster tokens. Constructing the hazard does **not** start combat, create an ordinary creature roster, roll encounter distance, determine surprise, advance time, consume a wandering-monster check, or override Kai Besil/module encounter cadence.

### Contact and holding

A referee-facing contact hook now represents a character actually moving into or through one live square:

```text
dev dmr2 grab grass contact <character> | square=<n> [| hazard=<id>]
```

Contact creates the source-defined hold automatically. No attack roll, saving throw, or contact damage is invented because the source supplies none. The character's held state records the hazard and square, and the square records its occupants. While at least one represented character remains held, the patch is exposed as the pending wilderness hazard; that pending marker clears when no represented victims remain.

### Strength-based per-round escape

The explicit escape hook is:

```text
dev dmr2 grab grass escape <character>
```

It resolves one per-round source attempt using exactly the printed probability: **5% for Strength 12 or lower**, then +5 percentage points per Strength point above 12 (for example Strength 16 = 25%). A successful attempt releases that character and updates both character and hazard state. The adapter does not add damage, action penalties, assistance rules, cutting modifiers, or other escape methods that the represented source does not specify.

### Per-square destruction

Already-adjudicated damage can be applied to a represented square with:

```text
dev dmr2 grab grass damage <square> <damage> [hazard-id]
```

This command deliberately does **not** make an attack roll or decide whether an attack can reach the grass. It only records damage after that question has already been adjudicated. Damage accumulates on the selected square; exactly **8 cumulative hp** destroys that square. Any represented characters held in the destroyed square are released. When every represented square is destroyed, the entire patch becomes inactive/resolved and no stale pending hazard remains.

Inspection is available through:

```text
dev dmr2 grab grass status [hazard-id]
```

### Nonnumeric wilderness review updated

The five-route v0.4.222 review remains intact, but Grab Grass is now classified as a **source-specific live area-hazard path when explicit area is supplied**. Its row remains nonnumeric. Together with the two Strangle Vine routes, the review now reports **3 source-specific constructible routes, 1 plan-only route (Buccaneer/Pirate), and 1 dynamic route (Ghostly Horde)** without manufacturing a Number Appearing total.

### Regression coverage and acceptance validation

Four new v0.4.223 regressions were added, raising the integrated suite from **1176 to 1180 tests**. They verify: (1) explicit-area construction with `n/a` provenance and no ordinary combat roster; (2) automatic contact hold with no invented hit/save/damage procedure; (3) the exact 5% Strength-12 and 25% Strength-16 escape probabilities; and (4) cumulative 8-hp square destruction, occupant release, and whole-patch resolution.

Two older regression assertions were updated so the newly explicit Grab Grass area path is not mistaken for a fabricated numeric roster, and two older stochastic tests were seeded inside the harness so acceptance runs remain deterministic. These changes alter test reproducibility only, not game rules.

Acceptance validation on the final v0.4.223 production logic produced:

- **1180/1180** complete core tests passed with `isolationPreserved:true`;
- four independent fresh-Chromium slices each passed **295/295**, together covering the full 1180-test suite again;
- every accepted slice reported `isolationPreserved:true`;
- **0** page/runtime exceptions and **0** console-error messages in the accepted full run and all four accepted slice runs;
- a separate uninstrumented production-JavaScript boot check reported **0** page/runtime exceptions and **0** console-error messages;
- extracted production JavaScript passes `node --check`;
- production HTML contains no `__kwHarness`, `__KW_TEST__`, or `__KW_SLICE__` instrumentation.

The current Chromium environment blocks direct `file://` navigation, so browser validation loads the exact production HTML shell and exact production inline JavaScript through Playwright's document-content path. Test-only harness exposure is injected into a separate JavaScript copy and is not present in the delivered HTML.
