### Leveller source profile

The implementation preserves the dedicated AC9 Leveller statistics from printed p. 73 (PDF p. 74):

- **Armor Class 1**;
- **Hit Dice 45\*\***;
- **Move 120' (40')**;
- **Attacks: 3 trunks or 2 tusks / 1 stomp**;
- **Damage: 6d8 ×3 or 6d10 ×2 / 1d100 or death**;
- **No. Appearing: 0 (1-3)**;
- **Save As: Fighter 36**;
- **Morale 11**;
- **Treasure Type: Nil**;
- **Intelligence 2**;
- **Alignment Neutral**;
- **XP Value 24,500**.

AC9 describes the Leveller as a sickly-green elephantine creature of roughly twice normal elephant height, with **two tusks, eight trunks, and four broad feet**. Each foot is explicitly **10 feet across**. The source gives no formal BECMI size code, so the runtime's `large` geometry classification is an engine spatial representation rather than a quoted AC9 statistic; the printed AC and attack rules remain authoritative.

The alias **Bodendruker** now resolves to the same supplemental runtime profile as **Leveller** instead of creating a duplicate creature identity.

### Eight trunks are independent AC 3 / 50 hp appendages

AC9 gives the Leveller **eight trunks**, but permits only **three new trunk attacks per round**, with a maximum of **one trunk per opponent**. v0.4.207 represents all eight trunks as separate appendages so the source's attack, hold, and damage rules can coexist without reducing the body's 45-HD hit-point pool.

Each trunk has:

- **Armor Class 3** when deliberately attacked;
- **50 hit points**;
- hit points tracked independently from the Leveller's body;
- a persistent hold record when it successfully grasps a victim.

A successful trunk Hit roll inflicts the printed **6d8** damage and also grasps the surviving victim. The engine does **not** add a second squeeze packet in the same round merely because the trunk just hit. Beginning on later rounds, every still-attached holding trunk inflicts **6d8 automatic squeeze damage once per round** without another Hit roll. All eight trunks can therefore maintain squeezes simultaneously even though only three trunks can make new attacks in one round.

The squeeze ends only when the relevant trunk is detached or the Leveller is slain. AC9 supplies **no victim escape saving throw, Strength contest, attack penalty, movement penalty, numerical trunk reach, or random voluntary-release chance**, so none is invented. An ally attacking a represented holding trunk uses its printed AC 3 and 50-hp appendage pool. Reducing that trunk to 0 hp detaches it, releases its victim, and leaves body hit points unchanged.

### Tusks, trample, and attack-mode boundary

The prose says the Leveller tries to trample opponents with its feet while attacking with either its **two tusks** or **three trunks**. The runtime therefore resolves one stomp/trample opportunity together with one of those two attack modes:

- tusk mode makes up to **two** ordinary Hit rolls for **6d10** damage each;
- trunk mode makes up to **three** new trunk Hit rolls, still respecting the one-trunk-per-opponent limit;
- existing trunk squeezes are separate continuing effects and resolve once on later rounds.

AC9 does not provide a die roll or decision table for choosing tusks versus trunks. The runtime defaults to trunk mode when at least one legal new trunk target exists, otherwise tusks, while allowing the referee/AI to set an explicit `levellerAttackMode`. This is an **engine tactical default**, not an additional AC9 rule.

### Stomp preserves the hit → Death Ray save → death-or-1d100 sequence

Each foot is 10 feet across. The printed trample procedure is represented literally:

1. the Leveller first makes its trample Hit roll;
2. only after a hit does the victim make **Save vs. Death Ray**;
3. on a failed save, the victim **dies, flattened**;
4. on a successful save, the victim instead takes **1d100 damage**.

A failed save is a direct source-defined death effect rather than ordinary hit-point damage, so it does not get converted into a normal damage packet first.

AC9 further states that **all flattened equipment, even magical gear, is ruined**. The engine therefore removes the victim's represented personal carried inventory and readied weapon/armor/shield records from usable equipment and archives them as ruined flattened gear. Represented magical bonuses on those records are not protected from the flattening rule.

There is an explicit data-model boundary: shared party inventory/funds, spell knowledge represented abstractly rather than as a located physical book, and separately modeled artifact records whose exact physical location is not encoded on the character are **not silently destroyed** merely because they are not provably beneath the foot. Those cases remain referee-resolved rather than inventing a location that the save file does not contain.

### Poison and normal-fire/cold immunities remain narrow

The source says Levellers are immune to **all poisons** and to **normal fire and cold**. v0.4.207 therefore blocks represented poison damage and ordinary nonmagical/non-breath fire or cold damage.

The word **normal** is kept meaningful. The engine does **not** silently turn this into immunity to magical fire/cold or elemental breath weapons. A Fire Ball and a cold dragon breath, for example, remain capable of damaging the Leveller unless another rule independently prevents that damage.

### Historical index evidence remains immutable

The earlier DMR2 index reconciliation entry `Leveller|AC9` remains an **index-only / source-available-not-catalogued** historical record. v0.4.207 adds the Leveller through the supplemental runtime layer instead of rewriting the evidence that the original 600-record workbook did not contain a dedicated Leveller record.

- the stomp performs a Hit roll and then Save vs. Death Ray, failed saves kill and ruin represented carried/equipped magical or mundane gear, while successful saves take exactly **1d100** damage;

## v0.4.206 — AC9 Huptzeen supplemental configurable construct profile

This bounded checkpoint implements **only the AC9 Creature Catalogue Huptzeen** from the source-gap ledger. It does not begin Leveller (Bodendruker), Oard, Phygorax, Possession, Reflecter, Sacrol, Stalwart, Vapor Ghoul, or any other remaining AC9 profile. The authoritative **600-record** creature catalogue remains unchanged.

The supplemental source layer now contains **twelve** records: the ten Rules Cyclopedia/source-gap supplements completed through v0.4.204, AC9 Agarat from v0.4.205, and `AC9X-HUPTZEEN` — **Huptzeen**. Runtime composition is therefore **619 profiles = 600 canonical workbook creatures + 12 supplemental source profiles + 7 Smoking Pillar module extensions**.

The twenty-profile source-gap ledger now reports **12 implemented / 8 remaining**. All ten Rules Cyclopedia gaps remain complete; two AC9 profiles are now represented, with the other eight AC9 profiles reserved for later bounded checkpoints.

### Huptzeen source profile

The implementation preserves the dedicated AC9 Huptzeen statistics from printed p. 27 (PDF p. 28):

- **Armor Class 3**;
- **Hit Dice 3**\*\* **to 7**\*\*\*;
- **Move (flying) 30' (10')**;
- **Attacks: Spells**;
- **Damage: By spell**;
- **No. Appearing: 1-3 (0)**;
- **Save As: Magic User 3-7**;
- **Morale 12**;
- **Treasure Type: See below**;
- **Intelligence 11**;
- **Alignment Neutral**;
- **XP Value: By HD (65 to 1,650)**.

The Huptzeen is represented as a **lesser construct** rather than as a humanoid combatant. It has no limbs, makes no physical weapon or natural attack, and moves only by its printed slow magical flight. The source allows forms ranging from jewellery and amulets to staffs, incense burners, and lecterns but gives no BECMI size code. The runtime therefore uses **Small only as an engine geometry default**, records that boundary explicitly, and does not present that size as an AC9 rule.

### Creator-derived spellcasting is configured explicitly instead of randomized

AC9 says that a Huptzeen's only attack is Magic-User spellcasting. Each day it can cast as many spells as a Magic-User of the same level as the construct has Hit Dice. Its spell set is fixed when the construct is made, it can never have more Hit Dice than its creator, and it cannot cast a spell its creator does not know.

The source does **not** provide a random table for Hit Dice, creator identity/level, creator spell knowledge, or the fixed Huptzeen spell set. v0.4.206 therefore refuses to fabricate those choices. Spawning a Huptzeen requires an explicit configuration containing:

- selected **Hit Dice 3-7**;
- creator level, which must be at least the selected Hit Dice;
- the represented creator's Magic-User spells known;
- the Huptzeen's fixed creation-time spell loadout.

The daily loadout must exactly fill the ordinary BECMI Magic-User slot capacity for the chosen Huptzeen level. This is necessary both to preserve the source's "as many spells as a magic user" daily capacity and to make the death explosion's **unused-spell count** deterministic. Spells outside the fixed creation loadout cannot be substituted later merely because the creator knows them. At the next campaign day, spent slots refresh, but the spell identities remain unchanged.

The engine supports normal represented Magic-User spell resolution for this fixed loadout and reuses the established low-level spell machinery where appropriate rather than creating a Huptzeen-only duplicate spell system.

### The 4-6 HD asterisk/XP transition is not silently invented

AC9 prints the Hit Dice range as **3**\*\* **to 7**\*\*\* and prints only the overall XP endpoints **65 to 1,650**. The available source text does not state at which intermediate Hit Die value the profile changes from two to three asterisks.

For that reason:

- 3 HD is fixed at the printed **two asterisks / 65 XP** endpoint;
- 7 HD is fixed at the printed **three asterisks / 1,650 XP** endpoint;
- for 4-6 HD, the configuration must explicitly provide **two or three special-ability asterisks**.

Once that source-context choice is supplied, the existing BECMI monster-XP progression determines the corresponding XP value. The runtime records the choice as a parameter-resolution boundary so the intermediate value is not misrepresented as verbatim AC9 text.

### Mind-affecting immunity and nonmagical-weapon resistance remain narrow

The source states that Huptzeens are immune to **mind-affecting spells**, explicitly giving sleep, charm, and hold as examples. The runtime therefore applies the existing represented mind-affecting-spell classification to Huptzeens while leaving ordinary damaging and non-mental magic unaffected.

The printed weapon defense is also implemented literally: **nonmagical weapons inflict half damage**. Magical weapon attacks deal their ordinary represented damage, and non-weapon damage such as environmental effects or spell damage is not halved merely because the target is a construct. No broader generic construct immunity is inferred.

### Death explosion and fragment value

When a Huptzeen reaches **0 or fewer hit points**, it explodes. The runtime now resolves the printed procedure directly:

1. roll **1d6** base damage;
2. add **2 damage for every unused spell** still available in that day's fixed loadout;
3. apply the result to **everyone within 10 feet** of the Huptzeen using represented combat geometry;
4. each victim makes **Save vs. Dragon Breath**; a successful save halves the damage;
5. record the explosion as resolved so the same death cannot explode twice.

The source also says the materials used to construct a Huptzeen cost at least **5,000 gp per Hit Die**, while fragments left after the explosion are worth only **1d4 × 50 gp per Hit Die**. v0.4.206 records the minimum construction cost on the configured instance and rolls/stores the surviving fragment value when the construct explodes.

### Historical index evidence remains immutable

The earlier DMR2 index reconciliation entry `Huptzeen|AC9` remains an **index-only / source-available-not-catalogued** historical record. v0.4.206 adds the Huptzeen through the supplemental runtime layer instead of rewriting the evidence that the original 600-record workbook did not contain a dedicated Huptzeen record.

This bounded checkpoint implements **only the AC9 Creature Catalogue Agarat** from the source-gap ledger. It does not begin Huptzeen, Leveller, Oard, Phygorax, or any other AC9-specific creature. The authoritative **600-record** creature catalogue remains unchanged.

The twenty-profile source-gap ledger now reports **11 implemented / 9 remaining**. All ten Rules Cyclopedia gaps remain complete; the remaining nine are AC9 Creature Catalogue profiles reserved for later bounded checkpoints.

### Agarat source profile

The implementation preserves the dedicated AC9 Agarat statistics from printed p. 83:

- **Armor Class 4**;
- **Hit Dice 4+3***;
- **Move 90' (30')**;
- **Attacks: 2 claws / 1 bite + scream**;
- **Damage: 1d3/1d3/1d3**;
- **No. Appearing: 1d6 (1d8)**;
- **Save As: Fighter 5**;
- **Morale 11**;
- **Treasure Type B**;
- **Intelligence 4**;
- **Alignment Chaotic**;
- **XP Value 200**.

The creature is represented as undead and keeps three ordinary physical attacks: two claws and one bite, each for **1d3**. Unlike a ghoul, the Agarat has **no paralysis attack**. No ghoul paralysis is inherited merely because the source compares its appearance and habits to ghouls.

### Scream and temporary Energy Drain are a distinct reversible state

The AC9 scream is implemented as an additional source-defined attack rather than replacing the claw/claw/bite sequence. When an Agarat has at least one character within **20 feet**, it may scream **once per 10-minute turn**. Every represented character within that radius makes **Save vs. Spells**, using the engine's normal Wisdom saving-throw adjustment. A failed save applies **one temporary Energy Drain level for 1d4 turns**.

Multiple Agarat screams are cumulative. Each failed scream is stored as its own timed effect, so one drain can expire while a later drain remains active. Temporary drains are deliberately kept separate from the permanent `energyDrainHistory` / `energyDrainLevelsLost` pathway used by ordinary undead Energy Drain. While active, the victim's represented level, XP-derived level state, THAC0, saving throws, spell slots, and other advancement-derived fields are recomputed from the temporarily reduced level.

For post-Name levels whose fixed hit-point gain is deterministic, the corresponding fixed hit-point benefit is temporarily removed and restored. For pre-Name levels, the save file does not retain the historical Hit Die result for each lost level. v0.4.205 therefore records an explicit pending HP-adjustment boundary instead of inventing a die result that cannot be reconstructed. This is the same source-fidelity boundary already used by the engine's permanent Energy Drain implementation.

A victim temporarily drained of all life energy follows the Agarat-specific exception instead of the ordinary 1st-level Energy Drain death rule: the victim falls **unconscious for 2d6 turns and cannot be woken** during that interval. The unconsciousness timer is independent of the individual temporary drain timers, so recovered levels do not prematurely wake the victim.

Both campaign-time advancement and combat-round advancement expire the temporary states. One 10-minute turn is represented as 60 ten-second combat rounds, so the scream's once-per-turn limit remains the printed turn frequency even inside combat.

### Source defenses and turning behavior remain narrow

The Agarat profile implements exactly the printed special defenses:

- immunity to **sleep**;
- immunity to **charm**;
- immunity to **hold**;
- ordinary weapon attacks affect it only when the weapon is **silver or magical**;
- clerical turning resolves the Agarat **as a spectre**.

The silver-or-magic gate applies to weapon attacks and does not invent general immunity to spells, environmental effects, or non-weapon magic. Silver and magical weapons that qualify deal their normal represented damage; no reduced-damage rule is borrowed from unrelated monsters. The existing Turn Undead dispatcher now accepts an explicit source-defined `turnAs` profile value so this rule does not depend on name matching.

### Historical index evidence remains immutable

The earlier DMR2 index reconciliation entry `Agarat|AC9` remains an **index-only / source-available-not-catalogued** historical record. v0.4.205 adds a supplemental runtime profile instead of retroactively rewriting the evidence that the original 600-record workbook did not contain the AC9 creature.

## v0.4.203 — Rules Cyclopedia Living Iron Statue supplemental standalone profile

This bounded checkpoint implements **only the Rules Cyclopedia Living Iron Statue** from the source-gap ledger. It does not begin the Living Rock Statue or any AC9-specific creature. The authoritative **600-record** creature catalogue remains unchanged.

The supplemental source layer now contains **nine** records: the three Hydra variants from v0.4.197, Normal Human, Great Boar, Great Whale, Rock Python, Living Crystal Statue, and `RCX-STATUE-IRON` — **Living Iron Statue**. Runtime composition is therefore **616 profiles = 600 canonical workbook creatures + 9 supplemental source profiles + 7 Smoking Pillar module extensions**.

### Living Iron Statue source profile

The implementation preserves the Rules Cyclopedia Living Iron Statue statistics from printed p. 208:

- **Armor Class 2**;
- **Hit Dice 4* (L)**;
- **Move 30' (10')**;
- **Attacks: 2**;
- **Damage: 1d8/1d8 + special**;
- **No. Appearing: 1d4 (1d4)**;
- **Save As: Fighter 4**;
- **Morale 11**;
- **Treasure Type: Nil**;
- **Intelligence 7**;
- **Alignment Neutral**;
- **XP Value 125**;
- **Monster Type: Construct, Enchanted (Common)**;
- **Terrain: Any (especially Ruins)**;
- **Load: 2,000 en at full speed / 4,000 en at half speed**.

The common Living Statue rule remains narrow: the creature is **not affected by sleep spells**. No broader immunity is inferred or imported.

### Nonmagical iron/steel weapon sticking is represented after normal damage

The Rules Cyclopedia says the iron body can absorb iron and steel. A hit by a **nonmagical metal weapon still inflicts normal damage**. After the hit, the attacker makes the printed **Save vs. Spells**. On success the weapon remains usable; on failure it becomes stuck in the statue and **can only be removed if the statue is killed**.

v0.4.203 therefore resolves the sequence in this order:

1. the successful weapon hit applies its ordinary damage normally;
2. if the statue survived the hit, the engine checks whether the weapon is clearly a nonmagical metal weapon;
3. the attacker makes Save vs. Spells;
4. on failure one copy of that weapon is removed from the attacker's usable inventory/equipment and stored on the statue as a stuck weapon;
5. once the statue is actually killed, previously stuck weapons become removable and are returned to their living owner's carried inventory; they are **not automatically re-equipped**.

A killing blow does not create a persistent stuck state: once the iron statue is dead, the source restriction on removal has already ended.

### No invented absorption timer or mixed-material ruling

The source additionally says that a weapon left in the statue is **eventually** absorbed completely, after which nonmetal parts are ejected. It gives no number of rounds, turns, or other timing rule. v0.4.203 records that source fact as referee-facing metadata but deliberately adds **no automatic absorption timer, destruction deadline, or percentage chance**.

The current equipment catalogue also does not explicitly encode construction material for every weapon. To avoid silently inventing material facts, the automated check uses a deliberately narrow classification:

- clearly metallic weapon identities such as swords, axes, hammers, maces, daggers, and the cestus use the printed sticking save;
- clearly nonmetal identities such as clubs, staves, bows, slings, blowguns, nets, whips, and similar entries do not;
- mixed or construction-ambiguous entries such as spears/polearms remain a **referee boundary** unless explicit material metadata is present.

This classification is an engine representation boundary, not an added Rules Cyclopedia rule. Explicit future equipment material metadata can resolve those cases without changing the monster rule.

Magical status for this specific interaction is tested from the weapon's own represented enchantment, rather than from temporary effective attack bonuses supplied by unrelated effects. This prevents an external bonus from silently converting a mundane metal weapon into a permanently magical object for purposes of the iron-statue source rule.

### Source-family isolation

The iron-specific weapon rule is attached only to `living_iron_statue`. It is **not** inherited by the Living Crystal Statue, and the still-unimplemented Living Rock Statue remains a separate source gap. ## v0.4.201 — Rules Cyclopedia Rock Python supplemental standalone profile

This bounded checkpoint implements **only the Rules Cyclopedia Rock Python** from the source-gap ledger. It does not begin the three Rules Cyclopedia Living Statue profiles or any AC9-specific creature. The authoritative **600-record** creature catalogue remains unchanged.

Runtime composition is therefore **614 profiles = 600 canonical workbook creatures + 7 supplemental source profiles + 7 Smoking Pillar module extensions**.

### Rock Python is a dedicated profile, not another snake alias

The Rules Cyclopedia prints Rock Python as a distinct column in the Snake family. v0.4.201 preserves it as its own runtime identity with the published statistics:

- **Armor Class 6**;
- **Hit Dice 5* (L)**;
- **Move 90' (30')**;
- **Attacks: 1 bite / 1 squeeze**;
- **Damage: 1d4 / 2d4**;
- **No. Appearing: 1d3 (1d3)**;
- **Save As: Fighter 3**;
- **Morale 8**;
- **Treasure Type U**;
- **Intelligence 2**;
- **Alignment Neutral**;
- **XP Value 300**;
- **Monster Type: Normal Animal (Common)**;
- **Terrain: Any except Arctic**.

The source also describes the creature as a **30-foot-long** brown-and-yellow, spiral-scaled snake. `monsterTypeKey('Rock Python')` now resolves to the supplemental `rock_python` profile. No existing Giant Racer, Pit Viper, Sea Snake, Giant Rattler, or DMR2 Rock Rattler profile is overwritten or treated as equivalent.

### Bite-then-coil sequence is represented literally

The Rules Cyclopedia states that the Rock Python's **first attack is a bite**. If that bite succeeds, it coils around the victim and **constricts in the same round**. v0.4.201 therefore does not model “bite” and “squeeze” as two unrelated ordinary attack rolls.

The implemented sequence is:

1. make the ordinary Rock Python bite Hit roll;
2. on a miss, no squeeze occurs;
3. on a successful bite, apply **1d4** bite damage;
4. if the victim remains alive, establish the coil;
5. immediately apply the source's **2d4** squeeze damage in that same round.

While the coil remains active, later Rock Python attack opportunities apply **2d4 automatic squeeze damage** to the held victim without making another bite Hit roll. The python does not begin biting new targets while it is maintaining that represented constriction.

### No escape save, immobilization penalty, or random release rule was invented

The source says the 2d4 squeezing continues automatically **until the snake dies or releases the victim**. It does not print:

- a victim escape saving throw;
- a Strength contest;
- a percentage chance to break free;
- an attack or AC penalty for the victim;
- an explicit movement/action lock;
- a random probability that the snake voluntarily releases its prey.

Accordingly, v0.4.201 does **not** import an escape procedure from Giant Squid, Kraken, wrestling, or another constricting creature. The engine records the coil and its automatic damage only. Snake death stops further squeeze resolution; an explicit `releaseRockPythonConstriction(...)` helper is available for referee/AI decisions to release the target. This helper adds no new probability or player escape rule.

The attack path still uses the existing natural-melee Hit machinery, including represented melee reach, applicable attack modifiers, Weapon Mastery deflection, and contact contingencies. Those are general engine procedures; the Rock Python-specific sequence remains source bounded.

### DMR2 Open encounter routing is now closed for Rock Python

The DMR2 Open wilderness table's **Rock Python / 1d3** result (rolls 81-82) now routes to the supplemental `rock_python` profile. The table no longer leaves Rock Python unresolved or substitutes another snake.

The Open table now has only the three intentionally unresolved **variant-choice** rows already preserved by the source routing:

- Chevall;
- Dragon, Blue;
- Dragon, Gold.

The historical DMR2 index reconciliation entry `Rock Python|204` remains `source_available_not_catalogued`. This is intentional: that sidecar records the earlier audit state of the immutable 600-record catalogue. The live source-gap ledger separately records that a supplemental source profile has since been implemented.

### Creature-gap ledger and catalogue boundaries

The twenty-profile source-gap ledger now reports **7 implemented / 13 remaining**. The implemented supplemental profiles are:

2. Regenerating Hydra;
3. Sea Hydra;
4. Normal Human;

7. Rock Python.

Runtime composition is therefore **613 profiles = 600 canonical workbook creatures + 6 supplemental source profiles + 7 Smoking Pillar module extensions**.

### Great Whale is a dedicated profile rather than another whale alias

The Rules Cyclopedia prints Killer Whale, Great Whale, and Narwhal as separate columns under the Whales entry. v0.4.200 preserves the Great Whale as its own runtime identity with the published statistics:

- **Armor Class 6**;
- **Hit Dice 36* (L)**;
- **Swim 180' (60')**;
- **Attacks: 1 bite**;
- **Damage: 3d20**;
- **No. Appearing: 0 (1-3)**;
- **Save As: Fighter 18**;
- **Morale 10**;
- **Treasure Type: Nil**;
- **Intelligence 2**;
- **Alignment Neutral**;
- **XP Value 12,000**;
- **Monster Type: Giant Animal (Very Rare)**;
- **Terrain: Ocean**.

The supplemental profile exposes swimming movement at 60 feet per combat round and no land movement. Fighter-18 saving throws are resolved through the existing BECMI save helper. `monsterTypeKey('Great Whale')` resolves to `great_whale`, while neither the Killer Whale nor any other existing whale profile is overwritten.

### Great Whale swallow threshold is represented literally

The source states that a **man-sized or smaller** creature is swallowed whole when the attack die roll is **4 or more above the score needed to hit**. v0.4.200 adds the narrowly named `die_margin4` swallow trigger and deliberately evaluates the **raw d20 result against the required score**. Attack modifiers that make an ordinary bite hit do not artificially create a swallow, and a natural 20 does not automatically swallow when it is fewer than four points above the required score.

A successful swallow records the source's **3d6 acid damage per round**. The engine then reuses the already-established common BECMI swallowed-creature interior procedure (including the represented interior AC/escape framework) rather than inventing a second parallel swallowed state just for the whale. The Great Whale profile is the authority for the trigger, victim-size limit, and continuing acid damage; the common interior handling remains engine infrastructure.

### The 10% ship attack is automated, but ram success is not invented

The Great Whale entry states that these creatures will **sometimes (10%) attack ships, attempting to ram**, and that a **successful ram inflicts 6d6 hull points**. v0.4.200 represents the 10% decision once for the whale encounter when a seaworthy active vessel is present. A result of 01-10 selects the ship-ram behavior; 11-100 leaves the whale attacking individual targets normally.

The source does **not** state how the Great Whale determines whether that ram succeeds. The Rules Cyclopedia's general naval-combat ram roll describes a ship pilot ramming another target; v0.4.200 does not silently assign that pilot procedure to a 36-HD whale. When ship attack is selected, the whale therefore creates a pending referee-required ram instead of rolling an invented attack procedure.

A pending ram can be resolved explicitly with:

`dev great whale ram success`

or

`dev great whale ram fail`

Only an explicit successful ruling rolls and applies **6d6 hull damage**. This is treated as the whale entry's specific source override and is not converted through the generic “giant sea creature damage ÷ 5” structural-damage rule. Failure causes no hull damage.

### Extremely large Great Whales remain an explicit referee boundary

The source says extremely rare Great Whales may grow to **double or triple normal size**, with a corresponding increase in Hit Dice and damage, but supplies no probability and no exact numerical scaling procedure. v0.4.200 preserves that statement as source metadata only. The engine does not randomly create enlarged whales or guess how 36 HD and 3d20 should scale.

### DMR2 Ocean encounter routing is now closed for Great Whale

The DMR2 Ocean wilderness table's **Great Whale / 1d3** result now routes to the supplemental `great_whale` profile. The previously unresolved dedicated-profile boundary is removed. The Ocean table's remaining unresolved rows are now exclusively family/variant-choice cases rather than absent Great Whale mechanics.

The historical DMR2 index reconciliation entry `Great Whale|212` remains `source_available_not_catalogued`. That is intentional: the earlier sidecar records what was missing from the authoritative 600-record catalogue, while the live creature-gap ledger separately records that a supplemental source profile has subsequently been implemented.

Runtime composition is therefore **612 profiles = 600 canonical workbook creatures + 5 supplemental source profiles + 7 Smoking Pillar module extensions**.

### The Great Boar is its own source profile, not an alias of ordinary Boar

The Rules Cyclopedia prints Normal Boar and Great Boar side by side, and Great Boar has a materially different stat line. The new supplemental profile preserves the Great Boar entry as a separate runtime identity:

- **Armor Class 3**;
- **Hit Dice 10* (L)**;
- **Move 90' (30')**;
- **Attacks: 1 tusk**;
- **Damage: 2d8**;
- **No. Appearing: 1d6 (1d6)**;

- **Treasure Type: Nil**;

The profile uses the existing BECMI attack/save helpers for a 10-HD creature saving as F5, but it does not copy the ordinary Boar's AC, HD, damage, XP, or identity. `monsterTypeKey('Great Boar')` now resolves to the supplemental `great_boar` profile, while the canonical workbook record count remains exactly 600.

### Source charge damage is now represented through a narrow profile hook

The Boar entry states that a boar which can charge for **20 yards** before reaching its prey inflicts **double damage on a hit**. The combat engine already had a generic represented-charge marker for animal movement: a creature ordered to charge and moving at least 20 yards / 60 feet before reaching melee is marked `chargedThisRound`.

v0.4.199 adds a narrow `sourceCharge` profile rule and a single damage-stage helper. It does **not** make all monsters deal double damage when charging. Only a runtime profile carrying explicit source-backed charge metadata receives the multiplier. Great Boar currently carries:

- minimum represented charge distance: **20 yards / 60 feet**;
- damage multiplier: **x2**;
- application: **a successful tusk hit after that represented charge**.

A shorter approach does not set the Great Boar's charge marker and therefore cannot receive the multiplier. The implementation reuses the same `chargedThisRound` state already observed by the existing set-spear-versus-charge procedure, so the boar's offensive charge and the defender's anti-charge reaction are driven by one represented movement fact rather than unrelated flags.

The new damage hook is intentionally source-scoped. It does not infer a universal monster charge system from the Great Boar entry, and it does not grant the multiplier merely because the creature begins a round at range.

### Load, barding, and mount statements are preserved without inventing a taming subsystem

The Rules Cyclopedia gives Great Boar load capacities of **3,000 en at full speed** and **6,000 en at half speed**, with **Barding Multiplier x3**. Those values are preserved directly on the supplemental profile for future mount/load integration.

The source also says Great Boars are occasionally used as mounts by barbaric tribes. The profile records that mount use is possible, but v0.4.199 deliberately does **not** invent a universal purchase price, taming probability, training time, rider restriction, or acquisition procedure. `mountUse.automaticMountIntegration` remains false until a source-backed general procedure or a later explicit module rule supplies the missing lifecycle.

### Lost-world ecology remains descriptive metadata

The source describes Great Boars as huge, terrifying animals most often encountered in **lost-world settings**. That statement is retained in the source-backed special-rules text. It does not silently rewrite the campaign's terrain encounter tables or cause Great Boars to appear in every woodland table. Terrain remains `Woods`; encounter-table placement remains controlled by the relevant table or referee procedure.

That historical disposition describes the state of the authoritative 600-record catalogue at the time of reconciliation and is intentionally not rewritten after a supplemental profile is added. The runtime gap ledger and the historical catalogue audit therefore answer different questions without contradicting one another.

### Canonical catalogue and prior adapters remain intact

No canonical record is added, removed, renumbered, or replaced. The Normal Human adapter functions remain present and continue to require referee-selected 1-7 hp plus an explicit existing weapon. ## v0.4.198 — Rules Cyclopedia Normal Human supplemental NPC adapter

This bounded checkpoint implements **only the Rules Cyclopedia Normal Human source profile and its NPC/combat adapter**. It does not begin Great Boar, Great Whale, the three Rules Cyclopedia Living Statues, Rock Python, or any AC9 creature gap. The authoritative 600-record creature catalogue remains unchanged.

The supplemental source layer now contains **four** records: the three Hydra variants from v0.4.197 plus `RCX-HUMAN-NORMAL` — **Normal Human**. Runtime composition is therefore **611 profiles = 600 canonical workbook creatures + 4 supplemental source profiles + 7 Smoking Pillar module extensions**.

`RCX-HUMAN-NORMAL` is deliberately typed as `supplemental-source-npc-adapter`, not as a generic monster replacement. `RUNTIME_MONSTER_CATALOG_INDEX` exposes it as `spawnMode:'npc-adapter'` with `requiresConfiguration:true`, preserving the Rules Cyclopedia distinction between an ordinary nonadventuring person and classed NPCs, NPC Parties, or the broader Men encounter entries.

### Published Normal Human encounter statistics are preserved directly

The profile preserves the Rules Cyclopedia Normal Human entry without filling its deliberate referee choices with invented random tables:

- **Armor Class 9**;
- **Hit Dice 1-1 (M)**;
- **Move 120' (40')**;
- **Attacks: 1 weapon**;
- **Damage: By weapon**;
- **No. Appearing: 1d4 (3d20)**;
- **Save As: Normal Man**;
- **Morale 6**;
- **Treasure Type (P) U**;
- **Intelligence 10**;
- **Alignment Any**;
- **XP Value 5**;
- **Monster Type: Human (Common)**;
- **Terrain: Settled**.

The profile also uses the Rules Cyclopedia's separate **Normal Man** combat rows: THAC0-equivalent **19** from the monster attack table and saving throws **14 / 15 / 16 / 17 / 17** for death-or-poison, magic wands, paralysis-or-turn-to-stone, dragon breath, and rod/staff/spell respectively. These are not inferred from 1-1 HD; the source explicitly says the creature saves as Normal Man and the engine uses the published Normal Man rows.

### Hit points are selected by the referee, never rolled by the adapter

The Rules Cyclopedia explicitly instructs the DM to **select, rather than roll**, a Normal Human's hit points according to age, health, and profession, within **1-7 hp**. The new adapter therefore refuses direct combat instantiation unless the caller supplies an integer hit-point value in that range.

This is a source boundary rather than a missing randomizer. The engine does **not** turn `1-1 HD` into a die roll, does not use a fixed average, and does not invent an age/profession probability table. A blacksmith can be configured at the high end and a child or sickly person at the low end exactly as the referee judges appropriate.

### Weapon choice reuses existing equipment but remains an explicit referee selection

The source says a Normal Human has **one weapon** and deals damage **by weapon**, but it does not provide a random weapon distribution for the entry. Direct combat creation therefore also requires an explicit existing weapon ID from the engine's ordinary equipment catalogue.

Once configured, the combatant uses that real weapon through the existing NPC/equipment path. `applyMonsterInstanceLoadout()` is intentionally skipped for this adapter so generic monster loadout heuristics cannot silently hand the person a fabricated random weapon. Missing or invalid weapon configuration is a hard adapter error rather than an invitation to guess.

An optional profession label may be retained as referee metadata. Alignment can likewise be selected from Lawful, Neutral, or Chaotic when the referee wants a concrete individual; otherwise the source profile remains `Any` at the template level.

### Morale remains 6 unless the referee explicitly chooses otherwise

The source gives Normal Human **Morale 6** and separately notes that soldiers and other fighting men will have higher morale, but it does not specify one universal replacement value. The adapter therefore defaults to 6. It permits an explicit referee-supplied morale value only as individual NPC configuration; no automatic soldier bonus or random morale rule has been invented.

### Direct generic monster spawning is intentionally blocked until the NPC adapter is configured

`resolveMonsterProfileForSpawn()` now recognizes configured NPC-adapter profiles before ordinary parameterized monster handling. `createCombatMonster(type,index,spawnOptions)` passes the adapter options through and rejects an unresolved configuration with a clear error.

For the user-facing developer test-encounter path, attempting to start an unconfigured Normal Human encounter produces an explanatory refusal instead of rolling hidden hit points or weapons. The convenience helper `createNormalHumanNpcCombatant(index,config)` is available for source-compliant configured creation.

This does not alter NPC Party, classed humans, Men subtypes, retainers, specialists, or player characters.

### DMR2 Settled routing now resolves the source identity without auto-spawning it

The previously audited DMR2 Settled wilderness table contains **Normal Human / 3d20**. That row now resolves to the dedicated `normal_human` supplemental source profile and is marked `adapterRequired:true`.

This is intentionally a two-stage result:

1. the DMR2 lookup is no longer an unresolved creature-profile gap;
2. actual combat instantiation still requires the referee to select the individuals' hit points and weapons.

The table therefore gains correct source identity without using the encounter table as an excuse to invent details the Normal Human entry leaves to the DM.

### Creature-gap ledger advances without rewriting historical index metadata

The twenty-profile DMR2/Rules Cyclopedia/AC9 gap ledger now reports **4 implemented / 16 remaining**: Flying Hydra, Regenerating Hydra, Sea Hydra, and Normal Human are backed by supplemental runtime profiles.

The historical DMR2 printed-page index audits continue to retain their original `source_available_not_catalogued` dispositions as reconciliation evidence. Those sidecars describe what the 600-record catalogue contained when the index was audited; v0.4.198 does not retroactively mutate that evidence merely because a supplemental layer now supplies the missing profile.

## v0.4.197 — Supplemental source-profile registry + Rules Cyclopedia Hydra variants

This bounded checkpoint implements **only the first mechanical batch from the v0.4.196 creature-gap ledger**: the supplemental source-profile registry scaffold and the three Rules Cyclopedia Hydra variants. The canonical 600-record catalogue remains untouched. The new source-backed profiles are layered **after the 600 canonical catalogue records and before the seven Smoking Pillar module extensions**, producing **610 runtime profiles = 600 canonical + 3 supplemental + 7 module**.

The new `SUPPLEMENTAL_SOURCE_COMBAT_MONSTERS` registry contains exactly three records:

- `RCX-HYDRA-FLYING` — **Flying Hydra**;
- `RCX-HYDRA-REGENERATING` — **Regenerating Hydra**;
- `RCX-HYDRA-SEA` — **Sea Hydra**.

Each runtime record carries `catalogAuthority:'supplemental-source-profile'`, preserving a visible distinction from both the authoritative workbook catalogue (`workbook-600`) and module-specific extensions (`smoking-pillar-extension`). `RUNTIME_MONSTER_CATALOG_INDEX` now indexes all three layers without adding, deleting, renumbering, or rewriting any of the 600 canonical records.

### Shared Hydra body/head procedure is now parameterized from the source

All three supplemental profiles derive only the shared Hydra procedure from the represented Rules Cyclopedia Hydra: one Hit Die per head, **8 hit points per head**, one **1d10 bite per active head**, and Fighter saving throws at a level equal to the current rolled head/Hit-Die count. The actual head count is rolled when the creature instance is spawned and retained in combat state.

The engine also derives the variant XP award from the Rules Cyclopedia monster XP table rather than inventing a fixed value. The implemented mappings are:

- **Flying Hydra, 5–9 HD with two asterisks:** 425 / 725 / 1,250 / 1,750 / 2,300 XP;
- **Regenerating Hydra, 5–9 HD with one asterisk:** 300 / 500 / 850 / 1,200 / 1,600 XP;
- **Sea Hydra, 5–12 HD with no added asterisk:** the ordinary 5–12 HD base-XP progression.

Hydra bite availability now follows the source's eight-hit-point head structure: as current hit points fall through eight-point bands, the active bite count is reduced accordingly. This is kept separate from generic multiattack handling so the creature's number of attacks remains tied to its surviving Hydra heads.

### Flying Hydra remains source-faithful without borrowing Roc-only carry mechanics

The Flying Hydra supplemental profile preserves **5–9 HD**, normal Hydra ground movement, **180' (60') flying movement**, Mountain terrain, and the source's special swoop statement: it may swoop and attack with up to three heads, with each such head capable of carrying off a man-sized or smaller victim.

The carry-off portion is deliberately stored as source-specific Hydra metadata with `automationReadiness:'referee-required'`. This checkpoint does **not** route the Flying Hydra through the Roc/Thunderhead carrier transaction, because those existing systems contain creature-specific thresholds and assumptions not stated for the Hydra. The source behavior is therefore represented without manufacturing an unsupported trigger or success threshold.

### Regenerating Hydra has an independent three-hit-point regeneration procedure

The Regenerating Hydra supplemental profile preserves **5–9 HD**, Swamp terrain, and regeneration of **3 hit points per round**. Damage caused by **fire** or by wounds explicitly **seared with a brand** is tracked as nonregenerable and permanently reduces the ceiling available to regeneration until some separate source-supported effect changes the injury state.

This subsystem is intentionally independent from the ordinary Troll regeneration engine. A Regenerating Hydra therefore does **not** inherit the Troll's three-round delay, severed-part lifecycle, fire/acid morale behavior, or ability to rise again from 0 hit points. It simply heals up to 3 eligible wound points once per round while alive. Repeated processing within the same round cannot grant duplicate healing.

### Sea Hydra preserves the printed movement boundary instead of inventing a swim rate

The Sea Hydra supplemental profile preserves **5–12 HD**, the normal Hydra head/body rules, Lake/Ocean terrain, and the source statement that fins replace its legs and that it is otherwise the same as its land-dwelling cousins.

The source does **not** print a separate numerical swimming movement rate for this variant. The runtime profile therefore marks movement as referee-required rather than guessing a swim speed. This is a deliberate RAW boundary: the creature is now a distinct spawnable profile, but automated movement will not fabricate a value absent from the source.

### DMR2 encounter routing now uses the dedicated supplemental variants

The previously audited DMR2 wilderness tables now route the two source-specific Hydra rows to their correct supplemental profiles:

- **River/Lake — Sea Hydra** resolves to `sea_hydra`;
- **Swamp — Hydra, Regenerating** resolves to `regenerating_hydra`.

The other unresolved or variant-required rows in those tables remain unchanged. No generic Hydra substitution is used.

`dev dmr2 gaps [name]` now reports implementation state as well as gap metadata. The reconciled ledger remains **20 distinct missing-profile targets**, but after this checkpoint it reports **3 implemented / 17 remaining**. `mechanicsAdded:false` remains a property of the historical ledger record itself; the new status fields separately expose the supplemental runtime implementations so the v0.4.196 audit invariant is not retroactively rewritten.

### v0.4.197 validation

Four new focused regressions were added for the supplemental registry, Hydra instance resolution, Regenerating Hydra wound/regeneration behavior, and save-normalization/gap-ledger persistence. Validation completed cleanly:

## v0.4.196 — DMR2 / Rules Cyclopedia source-available creature-gap ledger reconciliation

This bounded checkpoint performs **only the source-gap audit requested at the end of v0.4.195**. It does not add, replace, renumber, or silently reinterpret monster records. The completed DMR2 index reconciliation exposed source entries that are available in the current project but still do not have dedicated runtime catalogue profiles; this pass consolidates those entries into a single implementation ledger so later creature work can proceed without destabilizing the authoritative **600-record** catalogue.

The five DMR2 index-page audits contain **22 `source_available_not_catalogued` evidence lines**. Those lines represent **20 distinct missing source profiles**:

- **10 Rules Cyclopedia profiles**;
- **10 AC9 Creature Catalogue profiles**.

The difference between 22 index lines and 20 profiles is intentional. **Human, Normal / 197** and **Normal Human / 197** are two index labels for the same Rules Cyclopedia profile. **Statue, Living / 208** is a family heading that expands to the same three source-distinct Rules Cyclopedia profiles already individually indexed as **Living Crystal Statue**, **Living Iron Statue**, and **Living Rock Statue**. No evidence line is dropped, and no family heading is mistaken for a fourth statue creature.

`DMR2_RC_CREATURE_GAP_LEDGER` records the twenty source-backed gaps. `DMR2_RC_CREATURE_GAP_INDEX_MAP` maps every one of the twenty-two source-evidence lines to the corresponding gap record or records. `dmr2SourceAvailableCreatureGapEvidence()` re-derives the evidence from the completed printed-page 123-127 index audits rather than duplicating a hard-coded count. `dmr2RcCreatureGapLedgerStatus()` then checks the 22-to-20 reconciliation, the 10/10 source split, orphan mappings, unmapped evidence, implementation classes, and the unchanged catalogue size.

### The canonical 600-record catalogue remains authoritative and unchanged

The main result of this pass is architectural rather than mechanical. The gap ledger explicitly recommends a **supplemental source-profile registry merged at runtime after the authoritative 600-record catalogue**. This lets a later checkpoint add source-backed profiles without renumbering the existing records or rewriting previously audited catalogue identity.

The checkpoint therefore keeps all of the following true:

- `Object.keys(MONSTER_CATALOG_INDEX).length === 600`;
- `Object.keys(CATALOG_COMBAT_MONSTERS).length === 600`;
- `canonicalCatalogueChanged:false`;
- `mechanicsAdded:false`.

No AC, Hit Dice, attacks, XP, encounter actions, spell loadouts, turning behavior, or spawn mechanics are created by the ledger itself. The summaries in the ledger describe **what a future implementation must preserve from the cited source**, not executable monster mechanics.

Developer/referee inspection added:

```text
 dev dmr2 gaps [name]
```

Without a name, the command reports evidence/profile counts, source split, implementation-class counts, catalogue count, and the recommended supplemental integration layer. With a name it inspects the matching gap record, its source page, the DMR2 index evidence that exposed it, the existing catalogue records that may safely supply reusable primitives, and the required integration path.

### Three Rules Cyclopedia Hydra variants can derive from the represented Hydra without collapsing their identities

**Flying Hydra, Regenerating Hydra, and Sea Hydra** are classified as `derived_variant_profile`. The represented ordinary Hydra **EXP-0053** supplies the shared Hydra body/head rules, but each source variant still requires its own supplemental profile.

- **Flying Hydra** retains the Rules Cyclopedia 5-9 HD variant, 180' (60') flying movement, and its swoop/carry-off behavior.
- **Regenerating Hydra** retains 5-9 HD and regeneration of 3 hp per round, while fire damage and wounds seared by a brand do not regenerate.
- **Sea Hydra** keeps the source statement that fins replace legs and otherwise uses the land-hydra rules, with Lake/Ocean terrain. The ledger deliberately does **not** invent an unspecified swim speed.

These are source-backed derivations, not aliases to ordinary Hydra. The current encounter/index logic can therefore continue to mark them as dedicated-profile gaps until the supplemental profile layer exists.

### Normal Human belongs in an NPC adapter rather than a generic monster substitution

**Normal Human** is classified as `npc_adapter_profile`. The engine already has human/NPC abilities, equipment handling, weapon attacks, and Normal-Man saving concepts, so creating an unrelated monster surrogate would duplicate existing systems. What remains missing is the Rules Cyclopedia encounter/spawn adapter for the dedicated profile: AC 9, 1-1 HD, source-selected 1-7 hp, and the other source encounter values.

The two DMR2 index labels **Human, Normal / 197** and **Normal Human / 197** both map to this one planned adapter. NPC Party, classed humans, and other Men profiles remain distinct and are not substituted.

### Six Rules Cyclopedia profiles have local reusable mechanics but still require distinct source records

Six gaps are classified as `standalone_profile_local_hooks`:

- **Great Boar** — ordinary Boar **MON-0016** supplies family/charge primitives, but the distinct 10-HD Great Boar profile remains absent;
- **Great Whale** — existing whale-family records provide aquatic/large-creature primitives, but the 36-HD Great Whale, its swallow threshold and internal acid damage, and its ship ram remain a distinct profile;
- **Living Crystal Statue** — reuse the existing construct/living-statue framework, but do not replace it with DMR2 Jade/Rock-Ooze/Silver/Steel statues;
- **Living Iron Statue** — requires the Rules Cyclopedia weapon-sticking rule in addition to its own statistics;
- **Living Rock Statue** — source-distinct from DMR2 Rock/Ooze and requires the magma attack behavior;
- **Rock Python** — existing snake/constriction patterns can be reused, but the Rules Cyclopedia 5-HD constrictor is not interchangeable with the represented racer, rattler, cobra, or sea-snake profiles.

This classification means their mechanics are not wholly novel, but a dedicated source profile is still required. It prevents the tempting but incorrect shortcut of silently routing Great Whale to another whale, Rock Python to another snake, or the Rules Cyclopedia statues to DMR2's different living-statue family.

### Nine AC9 creatures need dedicated bespoke hooks

Nine AC9 gaps are classified as `standalone_profile_bespoke_hooks` because ordinary combat primitives cover only part of their source behavior:

- **Agarat** — scream-based temporary energy drain, cumulative unconsciousness at total drain, silver/magical weapon restriction, undead immunities, and spectre-equivalent turning;
- **Huptzeen** — a spellcasting construct with a fixed creator-derived magic-user loadout, construct defenses, nonmagical-weapon damage reduction, magical flight, and a death explosion based on unused spells;
- **Leveller (Bodendruker)** — independent trunk grapples/squeeze, destructible trunks, lethal/1d100 stomp handling and equipment destruction, plus source immunities;
- **Oard** — mind/magic defenses and source-defined technological devices used as creature equipment rather than unrestricted player magic items;
- **Phygorax** — ESP-driven full-sensory illusion bait, spine-contact energy drain, magic defenses, turning, and its transformation consequence;
- **Reflecter** — HD-scaled lightning geometry plus spell reflection, exceptional weapon resistance, wish vulnerability, and post-death shell behavior;
- **Sacrol** — two independent mist extensions, level drain plus continuing choke, limited same-creature-type undead control, and spectre-equivalent turning;
- **Stalwart** — normal weapon combat plus its defining challenge/competition procedure using d10 with Strength, Dexterity, or both and the associated tribute/service stakes;
- **Vapor Ghoul** — AC9's *Vapour Ghoul*: magical-damage gate, wraith-equivalent turning, mind-paralysis that continues the current activity, Intelligence loss, temporary insanity at Intelligence 0, and gradual Intelligence recovery.

These source summaries are retained as implementation requirements only. This checkpoint deliberately does not convert them into partial creatures that would appear spawnable before their special rules exist.

### Possession requires a hosted-entity lifecycle rather than an ordinary free-standing monster record

**Possession** is the single `hosted_entity_model` gap. AC9 describes an undead entity that inhabits a precious object, derives important combat properties from that host, can animate or use the object's abilities, attempts control of a victim, and can be forced out into a temporary shadow-cloud state before finding a new host or dissolving.

Representing that creature as a normal independent monster row would lose the source's defining behavior. Its eventual implementation therefore needs both a supplemental profile and an explicit host-object lifecycle. The ledger isolates this architectural dependency now so that the future catalogue expansion does not encode a knowingly incomplete surrogate.

### Reconciled implementation-class totals

The twenty profiles now have one and only one implementation class:

- **3** `derived_variant_profile`;
- **1** `npc_adapter_profile`;
- **6** `standalone_profile_local_hooks`;
- **9** `standalone_profile_bespoke_hooks`;
- **1** `hosted_entity_model`.

These classifications describe implementation work, not monster frequency or rules priority.

Four deterministic v0.4.196 regression groups were added, increasing the core suite from **1068 to 1072 tests**. They verify: (1) all **22** source-evidence lines consolidate to exactly **20** profiles with the **10 Rules Cyclopedia / 10 AC9** split and no mutation of the 600-record catalogue; (2) the duplicate Normal Human labels collapse to one profile while the Living Statue family heading expands to exactly Crystal/Iron/Rock; (3) the implementation classes remain exactly **3/1/6/9/1**, all three Hydra variants retain **EXP-0053** as their derivation base, Normal Human retains the NPC-adapter path, and Possession remains a hosted entity; and (4) source/path boundaries for the animal, statue, snake, and AC9 gaps remain explicit rather than becoming substitutions.

## v0.4.191 — DMR2 D&D Game Creature Index reconciliation, printed page 123

This bounded checkpoint reconciles **only the first printed page of DMR2's D&D Game Creature Index: printed page 123 (PDF page 124)**. It does not import the next index page and it does not create monster mechanics from an index citation. DMR2 explicitly presents this section as a cross-reference: plain entries point to Rules Cyclopedia creatures, bold entries point to creatures described in DMR2, and source abbreviations point to other products. The implementation therefore treats the index as **identity/provenance metadata**, not as a stat block.

The page contains **117 index lines**, preserved in printed order from **Actaeon / 156** through **Deadly Sphere / 162**. `DMR2_CREATURE_INDEX_PAGE_123` records the printed name, printed reference, printed-page/PDF-page provenance, and source identity without rewriting the source labels.

### Page-123 reconciliation is complete without expanding the canonical catalogue

`dmr2CreatureIndexPage123Resolution()` reconciles each source line against the existing authoritative **600-record** monster catalogue. `dmr2CreatureIndexPage123Status()` audits the whole page and reports the following mutually exclusive outcomes:

- **77 resolved_direct** — the source line matches an existing represented record directly or by unambiguous token-order equivalence;
- **16 resolved_alias** — an explicit narrow bridge connects the index wording to one represented catalogue record;
- **16 family_required** — the index line names a family or shared source entry represented by multiple distinct runtime profiles, so no member is silently selected;
- **8 index_only** — DMR2 points outside the currently represented 600-record catalogue and the index itself supplies no mechanics;
- **0 unresolved** — every line on this bounded source page has an audited disposition.

The status contract records `mechanicsAdded:false` and `catalogueRecordCount:600`. This checkpoint therefore changes neither combat statistics nor the canonical catalogue population.

Developer/referee inspection added in this checkpoint:

```text
 dev dmr2 index 123 [name]
```

Without a name, the command summarizes the page-level reconciliation counts and verified metadata discrepancies. With a name, it inspects matching source rows, preserving duplicate labels when their printed references differ.

### Narrow aliases preserve source wording without duplicating creatures

Sixteen explicit page-local aliases cover cases where the DMR2 index uses a synonym, subtype title, shortened name, or reversed family wording while the represented runtime identity is unambiguous:

- **Aerial Servant / 157 → Aerial Servant (Haoou)**;
- **Amir / 174 → Efreeti, Greater (Amir)**;
- **Apparition / 199 → Phantom, Apparition**;
- **Banshee / 182 → Haunt, Banshee**;
- **Bass, Giant / 177 → Fish, Giant Bass**;
- **Blackball / 162 → Blackball (Deadly Sphere)**;
- **Brigand / 193 → Man, Brigand**;
- **Buccaneer / 193 → Man, Buccaneer**;
- **Carp, Gargantua / 39 → Fish, Giant, Carp (Gargantua)**;
- **Carrion Crawler, Gargantuan / 177 → Gargantua, Carrion Crawler**;
- **Catfish, Giant / 39 → Fish, Giant, Catfish**;
- **Cave Toad / 209 → Toad, Rock or Cave**;
- **Caveman / 196 → Neanderthal**;
- **Coin-Sith / 30 → Dog, Elven**;
- **Colddrake / 173 → Drake, Colddrake**;
- **Deadly Sphere / 162 → Blackball (Deadly Sphere)**.

These bridges are reconciliation metadata only. They do not clone or alter the routed monster records.

### Generic index headings remain families where the source does not choose a subtype

Sixteen index lines deliberately resolve to a represented family rather than to one arbitrary member: **Air Elemental; Amber Dragon; Animal, Prehistoric; Archon; Bat; Bear; Beetle, Giant; Bird, Piranha; Black Dragon; Blue Dragon; Cat, Great / 18; Cat, Great / 163; Chevall; Crocodile; Crow; and Crystal Dragon**.

This preserves meaningful source distinctions. For example, **Cat, Great / 18** is DMR2's own six-profile Great Cat entry, while **Cat, Great / 163** is the Rules Cyclopedia five-profile Great Cat family. Likewise, the generic dragon headings do not choose Small, Large, or Huge, and **Air Elemental / 175** does not choose Staff, Device, or Spell Hit Dice.

### External/index-only references do not manufacture stat blocks

Eight page-123 lines remain deliberately `index_only` because the existing 600-record catalogue has no corresponding represented profile and the DMR2 index supplies only a pointer: **Agarat / AC9; Animal Spirits / GAZ12; Archaeopteryx / HW; Auratus / M4; Aurochs / HW; Automatons of the Blacklore Valley / HW; Bison, Giant / HW; and Cave Bear / HW**.

**Agarat / AC9** is marked as a source-available-but-not-catalogued omission because AC9 is among the project's reference materials. The other entries remain external-source metadata in this checkpoint. No statistics are inferred from their names or references. `M4` is preserved exactly as printed for Auratus; the source code is not expanded from the printed-page-123 legend because that legend does not define it.

The duplicate **Cave Bear** lines are also kept source-distinct: **Cave Bear / 159** resolves to the represented Rules Cyclopedia Cave Bear, while **Cave Bear / HW** remains index-only. The reconciliation does not collapse the Hollow World citation into the ordinary Cave Bear profile.

### Three concrete cross-reference metadata discrepancies are recorded, not silently rewritten

Source checking against the Rules Cyclopedia verified three cases where the existing catalogue record's stored `secondarySourcePage` does not match the DMR2 index citation even though the creature identity is clear:

- **Amir / 174 → COM-0039**: catalogue metadata currently stores secondary page **169**; the verified Rules Cyclopedia printed page is **174**.
- **Apparition / 199 → COM-0020**: catalogue metadata currently stores secondary page **197**; the verified Rules Cyclopedia printed page is **199**.
- **Carrion Crawler, Gargantuan / 177 → COM-0005**: catalogue metadata currently stores secondary page **180**; the verified Rules Cyclopedia printed page is **177**.

`DMR2_CREATURE_INDEX_PAGE_123_REFERENCE_ISSUES` records the catalogue value beside the source-verified value. This checkpoint intentionally does **not** rewrite the 600-row authoritative workbook-derived data in place; it exposes the discrepancy for later catalogue-source cleanup while preserving all current mechanics and identities.

## v0.4.190 — DMR2 Woods Wilderness Encounter Table audit/integration

This bounded checkpoint integrates **only DMR2's explicitly headed Woods d100 wilderness table** on printed page 122 (PDF page 123). It is the final DMR2 wilderness terrain table. The rendered source page was treated as authoritative because the table is physically split across three columns: rolls **01-14** occupy the lower-left column, **15-58** continue through the center column, and **59-100** continue in the right column.

The source contains **80 rows covering every d100 result from 01 through 100 exactly once**. The implementation preserves every printed roll band, monster label, Number Appearing expression, and page provenance. Direct visual landmarks include **01 Actaeon / 1**, **02-03 Animal Herd / 3d10**, **12 Blink Dog / 1d6+3**, **15-16 Brigand / 1d4x10**, **29-30 Draco Lizard, Giant / 1d8**, **31 Dragon, Gold / 1d4**, **32 Dragon, Green / 1d4**, **41 Flitterling / 5d6x10**, **48 Huge Wood Spider / 4d4**, **59-60 Orc / 1d6x10**, **65-66 Pixie / 1d4x10**, **77 Strangle Vine / Special**, **94-95 Wild Man / 3d10**, **98 Wood Imp / 8d10**, and **100 Wyvern / 1d6**.

### Woods d100 routing is executable but remains source-only

`DMR2_WOODS_WILDERNESS_ENCOUNTERS` stores the complete source table. `dmr2WoodsEncounterEntry()` performs pure d100 lookup, `rollDmr2WoodsEncounter()` resolves ordinary Number Appearing expressions through the existing DMR2 dice-expression helper, and `dmr2WoodsEncounterIntegrationStatus()` audits exact d100 coverage plus runtime-catalogue resolution.

The **Strangle Vine** row prints Number Appearing as `Special`. `rollDmr2WoodsNumberAppearing()` preserves that as a successful source-defined nonnumeric result with `total:null`; no creature count is fabricated.

All Woods rows retain printed-page/PDF provenance **122/123**. `columnWrapAfterRolls:[14,58]` records the physical source layout without treating either column change as a page break. The lookup remains intentionally non-mutating: it does not start combat, create a pending encounter, advance time, consume a wilderness encounter check, or replace the active regional/module encounter procedure. DMR2's Woods table supplies only the encounter result and Number Appearing field; it does not itself define encounter-check frequency, encounter distance, surprise, reaction, or automatic Woods-context selection.

Developer/referee inspection added in this checkpoint:

```text
 dev dmr2 encounter woods [d100]
```

`dev dmr2 encounter wood [d100]` is accepted as the same command. Without an explicit d100, the command rolls the source table and Number Appearing. With a supplied d100 it inspects that exact row, including runtime routing and printed/PDF page provenance. `Special` is displayed as a source-defined nonnumeric result rather than as a fabricated total.

- **Brigand → Man, Brigand**;

- **Eagle → Eagle, Normal** — the Woods row's `1d8` matches the Normal Eagle wilderness value and DMR2 separately represents Great Eagle;
- **Elven Dog → Dog, Elven**;
- **Gakarak → Gakarak (Forest Brooder)**;
- **Huge Wood Spider → Spider, Huge Wood**;
- **Hunting Spider, Giant → Spider, Giant, Hunting**;
- **Pocket Dragon → Dragon, Pocket**;
- **Shroud Spider, Giant → Spider, Giant, Shroud**;
- **Tarantella → Spider, Giant, Tarantella**;
- **Wild Man → Man, Wild**;
- **Wolf → Wolf, Normal** — the same table separately lists Dire Wolf at rolls 26-27;
- **Wooddrake → Drake, Wooddrake**.

Two source rows deliberately remain **variant-required** because the Woods table names a dragon family without selecting among the engine's separately represented size profiles:

- **Dragon, Gold** — Small, Large, or Huge;
- **Dragon, Green** — Small, Large, or Huge.

**Animal Herd** resolves to the engine's generic authoritative Animal Herd record rather than inventing a particular herd species or size. Its source profile itself carries variable Hit Dice/damage by animal size; this encounter-table checkpoint does not choose a species that the d100 result does not name.

No Woods row is otherwise unresolved.

Most Ruins results resolve directly or through the engine's token-order catalogue matcher. Nine narrow runtime-only bridges are required where the wilderness table uses a shorter source name than the represented catalogue profile:

- **Shade → Phantom, Shade**;

## v0.4.176 — Yowler flight / baying / damage-gate closure

This bounded checkpoint implements the **DMR2 Yowler only**, using the final creature entry before DMR2 transitions into its Wilderness Encounter Tables. No encounter-table transcription or later cross-system work is included in this pass.

DMR2 gives the Yowler AC 0, 3+3** HD, 150' (30') ground movement, 270' (90') flying movement, one 2d4 bite, Magic-User 11 saves, Morale 10, Intelligence 4, Chaotic alignment, XP 100, and Cavern/Mountain/Open/Ruins/Woods terrain. The description states that its flight is magical. Its pack baying can be heard up to one mile away; characters within 90 feet make a Save vs. Spells each round or flee in panic until a save succeeds. Packs larger than five impose -1 per additional Yowler, to a maximum -10. A successful save makes that character immune to that particular pack while the character remains in its immediate vicinity. Yowlers can only be struck by silvered or magical weapons; a magical weapon inflicts only its magical plus, while a silvered weapon inflicts 1 point.

### Magical flight and ordinary bite remain in the common combat model

The canonical Yowler profile now explicitly preserves **30 ft/round ground movement** and **90 ft/round magical flight**. Because the common 3D positional layer already recognizes a monster's flying movement mode as elevation-capable, no separate invented flight toggle or aerial attack restriction was added. The Yowler retains its ordinary **2d4 bite** through the common monster attack procedure.

The source's nocturnal hunting, gloomy-cavern lairs, warm-blooded prey, and preference for demihuman meat remain descriptive behavior. This checkpoint does not invent mandatory AI target priorities, daylight penalties, or a requirement that a Yowler can only fight at night.

### Pack baying is now a round-start fear procedure

At the start of each represented combat round, a living character whose center is within **90 feet** of an active Yowler in the represented pack and who can hear the baying makes a **Save vs. Spells**. The 90-foot measurement uses actual 3D center-to-center distance rather than Influence-Sphere separation, because the printed rule is an auditory range from the creature rather than a melee-contact distance.

The current represented pack size determines the save modifier: no penalty for one through five active Yowlers, then **-1 for each active Yowler beyond five**, capped at **-10**. One save is resolved per affected character per round rather than one save per individual Yowler.

A failed save creates a persistent panic state. It enters the engine's existing hard action-lock / forced-flight layer, so the character uses the next movement opportunity to move away from the represented Yowler pack rather than attacking or casting normally. The source says the victim flees **until the saving throw is successful**, so a character who has already failed continues making the once-per-round save even after fleeing beyond the initial 90-foot effect radius. On the first successful save the panic state ends immediately.

A successful save also records immunity to that **particular represented pack**. DMR2 uses the phrase "as long as they remain within its immediate vicinity" but supplies no distance or time measurement for that phrase. The engine therefore does not fabricate one. Pack immunity is keyed to the represented pack and is bounded to the current combat encounter; it is cleared when that represented encounter ends. The audit records this explicitly as the engine's bounded representation of an otherwise unquantified source phrase.

The baying's **one-mile audible range** is retained in the canonical/source metadata and developer status. It does not itself force a save outside 90 feet; the source separately states that the fear save applies only within 90 feet.

### Silver/magical weapon damage gate is executable

Yowler weapon defense now occurs in the common monster-damage path:

- an ordinary nonsilver weapon cannot damage a Yowler;
- a nonmagical silvered weapon inflicts exactly **1 point** on a successful hit;
- a magical weapon inflicts damage equal to its represented **magical plus only**, ignoring its ordinary damage dice, Strength bonus, and other ordinary weapon damage;
- a represented magical weapon with no positive magical plus and no silver property inflicts 0 through this rule rather than receiving invented base damage;
- the rule is a weapon restriction, not blanket magic immunity, so ordinary spell damage is not discarded merely because it is magical.

This uses the silver-material flag already preserved in the common weapon damage context by the Wyrd checkpoint. No unrelated lycanthrope, undead, or enchanted-monster defense has been imported.

Developer/referee inspection added in this checkpoint:

```text
 dev yowler status [name]
```

The report exposes ground/flying movement, magical flight, audible/effect baying ranges, current active pack size and save modifier, failure/success behavior, the explicit unquantified-immediate-vicinity boundary, and the silver/magical weapon damage rule.

### Save/load and encounter lifecycle

The Yowler panic/immunity record is preserved by party-member normalization, including pack identity, source Yowler IDs/names, the current pack penalty, and recent save history. This keeps a mid-combat save/load from silently discarding the fear state or granting an extra save in the same represented round. When combat ends, the temporary particular-pack/immediate-vicinity record is cleared with the other encounter-local fear states.

### Regression coverage

Four deterministic v0.4.176 tests were added. ## v0.4.175 — Xytar breath / combat-choice closure

This bounded checkpoint implements the **DMR2 Xytar only**, using the Xytar entry on DMR2 PDF pages 117–118 (printed creature page 116), with AC9 used only as a secondary stat cross-check. Yowler and later catalogue creatures remain outside this pass.

DMR2 gives the Xytar AC 3, 5+1* HD, 120' (40') movement, one bite or one breath attack, 1d10 or 3d6 damage, Fighter 2 saves, Morale 8, Intelligence 4, Neutral alignment, XP 400, and Desert terrain. The combat paragraph defines a fire cone **30 feet long and 10 feet wide at its widest point**, requires the Xytar to **breathe on its first attack**, then close to use its jaws, and gives a **1–2 on 1d6** chance to breathe instead of biting once it is in melee.

### The opening breath is now mandatory and uses represented cone geometry

A represented Xytar begins combat with an opening-breath state. Its first attack resolves as the printed **3d6 fire breath** rather than a bite. The attack uses the engine's existing tapered-cone geometry at **30 feet long × 10 feet wide at the far end**, so every represented creature actually inside that cone receives the same rolled 3d6 breath packet. Creatures outside the cone do not take damage merely because they are near the selected target.

If the selected target is beyond 30 feet, the engine does not silently substitute a bite or consume the opening-breath requirement. The attack remains unresolved until a valid breath target/geometry exists. This preserves the source's mandatory first-breath instruction instead of inventing an alternate opening tactic.

The damage context is explicitly marked **breath / fire / cone**. That allows already-implemented rules which expressly protect against breath weapons to recognize the attack. It does not make the Xytar a dragon or import unrelated dragon abilities.

### No unprinted Xytar saving throw has been invented

Neither the DMR2 Xytar entry nor its AC9 predecessor states that the Xytar's 3d6 breath permits a saving throw or that a successful save halves the damage. The Rules Cyclopedia does state a save-for-half procedure in its **dragon** breath section, but that text is specifically describing dragon breath and the Xytar entry does not refer the reader to that procedure.

Accordingly, this implementation does **not** add an ordinary Save vs. Breath Attacks to the Xytar breath. The engine still honors defenses whose own rules explicitly apply to any breath weapon (for example an already-represented breath-weapon immunity/resistance), because the Xytar attack itself is expressly described as a breath weapon. This separates a defender's broad breath protection from an unsupported new saving throw granted by the Xytar entry.

### Printed close-then-choose behavior is executable

After the opening breath, a Xytar outside melee does not repeatedly fire from range. Its combat procedure records the source-defined next behavior as **close to use its jaws**. Actual movement remains in the normal positional movement system; this special attack routine does not teleport the Xytar or invent extra movement.

Once the Xytar is in melee, the engine rolls **1d6 each attack opportunity**. On **1–2** it breathes instead of biting. On **3–6** it makes its ordinary **1d10 bite** through the common monster-attack path, retaining the normal attack-roll, Armor Class, and other shared combat rules. The profile's preferred melee distance is now source-bounded to **close**, matching the creature's printed instruction to close and use its jaws.

Developer/referee inspection added in this checkpoint:


The report exposes whether the mandatory opener is still pending, the 30-by-10 cone and 3d6 fire packet, the explicit no-printed-save boundary, the 1d10 bite, the melee 1–2-on-d6 breath choice, and the most recent Xytar combat decision.
